Re-pulled 2026-09-16 after the DB pilot split (11 'Also:' -> 23; migration-v24), the QB Drop-Back pilot split (56 -> 84, Option B), AND the WR/TE/RB pilot split (40 'Also:' rows -> 51: 11 clean-IES split children [S1 hip-rotation, S3 break-stride, S4 chop-into-load, S5 out-of-bounds skip], 29 row-tag/held UPDATEs; the 3 S2 knee-flexion rows HELD unsplit — no authored IES manufactured). Fallback for checkpoints_v2_source.load_raw() when Supabase is unreachable; makes resolver tests reproducible.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced 2-point or 3-point stance with a minimal toe-to-instep stagger over the ball, securing immediate visual alignment on the head-up or shaded nose tackle.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Two-part signal reusing the established Stance-family design: (1) Stagger - horizontal distance between rear and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index), image plane, side view, torso-length scaled (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center). Coaching target: minimal/near-zero stagger. (2) Squareness - shoulder-line and hip-line horizontal-ness, front view, confirming a balanced, non-rotated base. NOTE: 'weight centered over the ball' is not measurable without ball tracking; this signal covers foot/torso geometry only, and needs both Side and Front footage to cover both sub-checks fully.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap the ball crisply while simultaneously executing an immediate post step or brace step, preserving a shoulder-width base with zero drop in height.
rows.fault_trigger: Ducking Head on Snap. Dropping the chin and breaking spine angle on the snap, losing visual tracking of the defender and surrendering leverage.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Three-part signal: (1) First-step latency - frame offset between the snap event and the first detectable ankle displacement past a small noise threshold. NOTE: this needs a ball/snap-frame reference the pose pipeline doesn't provide alone (needs ball tracking or a manually marked snap frame) - pose can detect WHEN the foot moves, not whether that lines up with the actual snap. (2) Base width retention - lateral ankle-to-ankle distance, confirming it doesn't narrow below the Phase 1 baseline. (3) Torso lean ('spine flat') - Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center angle vs. vertical, watched for a sudden drop. Knee flexion angle (Left/Right Knee) is directly measurable; 'zero drop in height' needs the pre-snap frame as a comparison baseline.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a wide, stable pocket wall immediately; sink the hips back into a quarter-squat, centering the imaginary nose tackle directly between both knees.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Hip height drop from the Phase 1 baseline (Pelvis Center vertical displacement) and knee flexion angle, confirming the sink into a lower base. Shoulder-line horizontal-ness (front view) confirms square framing. NOTE: 'defender framed between the knees' is NOT measurable - there is no real defender in this simulated rep, and even with one, single-subject pose tracking doesn't register a second person's position relative to the blocker's frame. This signal covers the blocker's own base/hip/shoulder geometry only.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot a compact, violent two-handed strike directly into the defender's chest plate with thumbs up and elbows tucked to absorb interior power.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Wrist-to-sternum closing distance and elbow-to-torso tuck angle at the strike frame, confirming hands drive inside and elbows stay tight rather than flaring. NOTE: 'thumbs up' hand orientation is not measurable by body pose - that's hand-landmarker territory, not wired into this checkpoint; 'maximum kinetic force' is not directly measurable, only wrist displacement velocity as a rough proxy (would need Needs Motion tier for that specific sub-signal, not attempted here).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sustain continuous 6-inch choppy steps into the turf, maintaining inside hand control and keeping the defender framed between the legs until the pass is released.
rows.fault_trigger: "Pop and Stop". Snapping the ball, landing initial contact, and freezing foot movement, allowing the rusher to effortlessly shed the block.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Continuous small-amplitude ankle displacement across the rep window (the 'churn'), confirming the feet never stop moving for an extended run of consecutive frames. Elbow angle stability confirms 'locked arms' (staying within a narrow range rather than collapsing). NOTE: 'anchor locked' as a defensive-pressure-resisting outcome isn't measurable without an actual opposing force; this only confirms the blocker's own footwork/arm-lock mechanics continued, not whether they successfully anchored against a real rusher.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced 3-point stance with zero to minimal toe-to-instep stagger, centering weight primarily over the balls of the feet for an explosive launch.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Reuses the Stagger design: horizontal distance between rear/front foot ground-contact points, side view, torso-length scaled. Coaching target: minimal/near-zero stagger. Secondary signal: knee-over-ankle forward lean angle as a rough proxy for 'weight centered over the balls of the feet' - pose can't measure actual foot-pressure distribution, only the resulting body lean, so this is an approximation, not a direct measurement.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Initiate forward displacement while cleanly executing the snap, firing downhill to split the nose tackle (0/1-technique) or laterally to cut off the A-gap before the defender can penetrate.
rows.fault_trigger: "Roll-Snapping". Rolling the shoulders forward over the toes during the snap, causing the center to lunge, lose balance, and get easily pulled down by the defender.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Two-part signal: (1) First-step onset timing relative to the snap - same limitation as pass-set: needs a ball/snap-frame reference the pose pipeline doesn't provide alone. (2) Direction of travel - Pelvis Center displacement vector over the first several frames, confirming a downhill (forward) vs. lateral burst matches the called play. Torso lean ('spine flat') - Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center angle vs. horizontal, confirming a flat, driving posture rather than standing tall. NOTE: needs both Front (lateral direction) and Side (torso flatness) coverage; single-angle footage only partially confirms this checkpoint.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the first power step directly through the crotch of the imaginary defender, framing the target tightly between both knees.
rows.fault_trigger: "Gazing". Raising the eyes early to look for second-level linebackers before cleanly securing the down-lineman first.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Lateral symmetry of knee/ankle position relative to Pelvis Center's forward path - confirms the blocker's own stride stays centered and square rather than drifting to one side. NOTE: 'defender framed between the knees' is NOT measurable - there is no real defender in this simulated rep, and single-subject pose tracking wouldn't register a second person's position relative to the blocker even if there were one. This signal covers the blocker's own stride symmetry only.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fire a violent, compact punch inside the chest/numbers using the off-hand immediately to establish dominant control, keeping elbows tightly tucked.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Wrist-to-sternum closing distance and elbow-to-torso tuck angle at the strike frame, confirming the punching hand drives inside with elbows tight. NOTE: this is a ONE-handed strike ('off-hand' punch), unlike Blocking-Pass Center's two-handed strike - pose alone can't determine which specific hand is the designated 'off-hand' without play-context, so track whichever wrist shows the dominant closing-distance spike. 'Maximum kinetic force' is not directly measurable, only wrist displacement velocity as a rough proxy (not attempted here).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition instantly from the initial power step into short, rapid 6-inch "chat steps" to drive the defender vertically.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Continuous small-amplitude ankle displacement across the rep window (the 'chat steps'), confirming the feet never stop moving for an extended run of consecutive frames - reuses the churn signal from Blocking-Pass Center's Finish phase. Forward Pelvis Center displacement over the same window confirms sustained forward drive (the Matrix's 'vertical displacement' means downfield drive here, not literal vertical movement).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Approach the line and straddle the midline of the ball, spreading your feet 4 inches wider than shoulder-width to build an unyielding, broad anchor. Keep your spine flat, your chest proud, and your belt line perfectly square to the line of scrimmage, remaining completely balanced.
rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base. Setting your feet at a standard shoulder-width. A narrow base during a shotgun snap destroys your balance, causing you to tip forward the moment you snap the ball.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a 0-inch stagger — a perfectly parallel base — with neither foot ahead of the other.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: feet should show no consistent vertical offset (0-inch stagger). NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips deeply and shift your weight heavily backward onto your heels, balancing your weight at 40% forward / 60% backward. Your cleats must stay flat and glued to the turf so you do not fall forward while snapping.
rows.fault_trigger: Fingertip Leaning. Placing forward pressure onto the ball. Leaning forward causes the ball to sail high or skip off the grass, leading to critical turnover fumbles.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach your dominant hand forward to grip the center of the ball. Extend your non-dominant hand forward, resting the forearm comfortably across your non-snap thigh to build a rigid upper structural frame.

Compress your lower joints. The millisecond the cadence hits, launch the ball backward using a violent wrist-snap while instantly stepping back with your lead foot to absorb the nose-guard's pass rush.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align with a square base, identifying the "triangle" (Nose tackle to the linebackers) to establish dual-threat awareness.
Secure the snap and take a diagonal 45-degree placeholder step toward the slide side.
rows.fault_trigger: Getting Caught in "No Man's Land". Staring at one specific defender while a blitzer slips through the vacated adjacent gap destroys the integrity of the half-slide protection. You must protect the zone, not chase the man.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes actively scanning the triangle to diagnose blitzing linebackers or interior line stunts.
If a threat enters the slide gap, engage immediately; if no immediate threat appears, proactively punch and assist the guard on the man-protection side.
Maintain the hinge block or double-team structure, ensuring the interior pocket remains deep and clean.
Identify the assigned 0-technique, 1-technique, or blitzing linebacker to lock head-to-head.
Secure the snap and execute a quick, vertical "Post Set" taking 1-to-2 short steps backward.
rows.fault_trigger: Lunging Forward. Firing out of your stance and leaning forward allows the defender to easily use a swim or club move to bypass you instantly.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a firm, immovable base by keeping the head back and the hips sunk low.
Deliver a violent, two-handed strike directly into the numbers of the interior defender.
Halt the defender's upward momentum completely and maintain the block until the pass is released.
Establish a square, parallel base under center, sinking the hips to prepare for the snap.
Immediately upon the snap, take a short, 6-inch lateral "brace step" with the foot closest to the slide direction.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-Stepping Laterally. Taking a brace step wider than 6 inches creates a massive gap between you and the backside Guard, or causes your hips to turn sideways, ruining your anchor.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Punch violently with the inside hand to intercept and control the designated A-gap.
Anchor the backside foot firmly into the turf to absorb sudden interior blitzes.
Maintain square leverage to ensure no defender crosses your face or compromises the slide line.
Identify the primary defensive lineman to double-team and locate the target second-level linebacker.
Secure the snap and take a hard, 45-degree "gallop step" directly into the hip of the defensive lineman.
rows.fault_trigger: Climbing Too Quickly. Abandoning the double-team to climb to the second level too early leaves the defensive lineman un-secured, allowing them to split the block and instantly disrupt the backfield.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lock your inside shoulder tightly against the adjacent guard's outside shoulder to eliminate any physical gaps.
Keep your eyes up and focused forward to track the assigned linebacker's path while driving the defensive lineman.
Detach and peel off to the linebacker only when their jersey numbers cross your field of vision, delivering a decisive block at the second level.
Establish a balanced, coiled stance with eyes locked on the assigned interior defender.
Secure the snap and fire out instantly with a low, explosive "power step" right through the crotch (midline) of the defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Stepping Narrow or High. Coming out of the stance with a narrow base or popping completely upright surrenders all leverage, resulting in you being violently pushed backward directly into the Quarterback's or running back's path.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Follow the initial strike instantly with a short "chat step" to establish a wide, anchored driving base.
Shoot the hands violently inside the defender's frame to gain inside leverage and chest control.
Maintain low leverage and drive the legs continuously using short, powerful movements to displace the defender vertically.
Identify the pull direction, the intended insertion gap, and the target linebacker assignment.
Secure the snap, push aggressively off the play-side foot, and take a lateral step backward with the backside foot to clear the line.
rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Hips and Running. Turning your hips and running like a sprinter blocks your vision of the second-level flow, makes it impossible to adjust to a linebacker's counter-movement, and leaves the backside open.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: "Skip" laterally behind the line of scrimmage while keeping the shoulders parallel to the end zone to maintain full vision of the defense.
Plant the outside foot and violently transition from lateral movement to a vertical sprint, inserting into the designated gap.
Engage the target linebacker the exact moment they commit, driving upward to clear the running lane.
Identify the penetrating defender designated to be trapped and mentally lock onto the nearest inside threat to down-block.
Secure the snap and take a sharp, heavy "down block" step at an inside angle directly away from the trapped defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Slowing the Timing. Allowing the purposefully bypassed defender to touch, chip, or slow you down in any way. You must clear the space instantly to allow your pulling teammate an unobstructed path to deliver the trap block.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Clear the path completely cleanly; do not make eye contact, attempt to chip, or engage with the defender being trapped.
Immediately seek out the next nearest interior defensive lineman or flowing linebacker down the line of scrimmage.
Engage the secondary threat with maximum force, pinning them inside to create a clean wall for the pulling player and ball carrier.

Approach the ball and straddle the midline of the football, spacing your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to create a highly stable, square anchor. Keep your belt line completely square to the line of scrimmage. Ensure your head is up, neck is relaxed, and chest is proud to comfortably see the defensive front and call out protections.

Approach the ball and straddle the midline of the football. Set your feet completely parallel (0-inch stagger / perfectly square), spaced slightly wider than shoulder-width apart to create a highly stable, square anchor.
rows.fault_trigger: Unconscious Stagger. Allowing one foot to drift backward out of a habit. Any stagger from the Center creates an offset gap under your hips, causing quarterback-center exchange fumbles.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Vertical (image-Y) position of each foot's ground-contact point (Heel/Foot Index) relative to the other, scaled by hip height as the reference for foreshortening. The foot appearing higher in frame (smaller image-Y) is the one staggered further back from the camera - an ordinary perspective artifact of a level, front-facing camera, not a depth estimate (no MediaPipe Z used). Gives ORDER (which foot is back) and a rough relative magnitude only, not a precise inch value - front view cannot resolve depth-axis distance precisely. Coaching target: feet should show no consistent vertical offset (0-inch stagger). NOTE: this is a deliberately weaker signal than the side-view version of this same checkpoint; use side view whenever available.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set your feet completely parallel — a 0-inch stagger, perfectly square — with neither foot ahead of the other.
rows.fault_trigger: Unconscious Stagger. Allowing one foot to drift backward out of a habit. Any stagger from the Center creates an offset gap under your hips, causing quarterback-center exchange fumbles.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling (shoulder width is a front-view-only scale unit). Coaching target: 0 inches / feet fully parallel - the rear and front ground-contact points should sit at the same depth. NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink your hips straight down into a deep squat, keeping your weight distributed evenly on the balls of both feet (50/50 balance). Do not lean heavily forward onto the ball, as this ruins your ability to handle a sudden defensive nose-guard rush.
rows.fault_trigger: Leaning on the Ball. Placing too much upper-body weight directly onto the football. If the ball slips, you will collapse instantly into the dirt.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach your dominant hand forward to grip the football cleanly along the laces. Extend your non-dominant arm forward, resting your elbow or forearm lightly on your non-snap thigh to lock in a rigid, structural framework.

Hold your position firmly as the quarterback rides directly under your hips. Keep your back completely flat and your ankles, knees, and hips flexed like a tightly compressed coil, ready to deliver a clean snap and immediately strike the defender.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: this measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - the 33 pose points give no mid-back landmark, so true rounding (an upper-back curve while the lower back stays fixed) is not directly visible, only whether the shoulder-to-hip line as a whole tilts further forward than at Stance Locking. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align in a comfortable stance with the left foot staggered back to set efficiently to the left B-gap or A-gap threat.
Execute a short, crisp angle set to the left, taking weight onto the inside leg (70/30 distribution) while keeping the base wide.
rows.fault_trigger: Opening the Gate. Bailing out too wide with the left foot and turning hips outward, opening a massive A-gap lane.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hips low and square, framing the incoming rusher directly between the legs to shut down counter moves.
Deliver an independent outside-pillar punch with the left hand into the defender's shoulder/chest, followed by the right hand under the chest plate.
Shuffle laterally in low, active short steps, constantly resetting the base to mirror the defender until pass release.
rows.fault_trigger: "Sticking the Cleats". Planting the feet heavy upon first contact, leaving the guard vulnerable to a quick arm-over or spin move.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Assume a powerful 3-point stance with a slight left-foot-back stagger (toe-to-instep) to anchor and push forward-diagonal paths.
rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing". Placing too much weight heavily onto the down hand for a drive block, or leaning back on the heels when preparing to pull, tipping off the defense.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Trigger an aggressive, forward angle of departure to act as an interior engine to physically displace defensive tackles and secure the inside gap.
Drive the feet wide apart on parallel tracks so the imaginary defender's core remains strictly framed between the guard's thighs.
rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base. Stepping too narrow on the second step, allowing the defender to easily push the guard sideways.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot both hands straight out from the dirt into the inside V of the chest plate, exploding up through the palms with thumbs up to lift the opponent.
Run the feet relentlessly on contact, keeping cleats low to the ground and continuously pumping forward to finish the block.
Take a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your right foot forward. Keep your spine straight, your chest upright, and your shoulders squared completely to the defensive line.
rows.fault_trigger: Pre-Angling Hips. Turning your lower body outward toward the perimeter before the snap. This tips off the defense to an outside zone run or a slide protection schema.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your left foot back exactly 3 to 4 inches, locking your left toe into a direct line with the mid-foot arch of your right shoe.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: left foot staggered back a moderate, visible amount (3-4in). NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drop your weight low and backward, locking in a 45% forward / 55% backward split, keeping the bulk of your power stored in your heels and core.
Drop your left hand to the turf into a light 3-point contact stance, using your fingertips solely for balance. Rest your right hand securely on your right thigh.
Hold a rigid, half-squat frame. Keep your ankles and knees bent like springs, completely uncommitted to a direction until the ball is snapped.
rows.fault_trigger: High Hips. Standing up too vertical in a 3-point stance. High hips strip away your lower-body power, allowing defenders to easily push you into the quarterback's face.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your right foot forward. Keep your spine straight, your chest upright, and your shoulders squared completely to the defensive line.
rows.fault_trigger: Pre-Angling Hips. Turning your lower body outward toward the perimeter before the snap. This tips off the defense to an outside zone run or a slide protection schema.

Drop your left hand to the turf into a light 3-point contact stance, using your fingertips solely for balance. Rest your right hand securely on your right thigh.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Identify the dual-threat defensive front, noting both the immediate interior gap responsibility and the potential outside looping threat.
On the snap, set at a controlled 45-degree angle to the left, keeping a perfectly balanced weight distribution on the balls of the feet.
rows.fault_trigger: Dropping Too Deep. Dropping too deep backward in the pass set abandons the line of scrimmage. This forces the pocket to shrink vertically, allowing the defensive line to easily compress the space around the quarterback and disrupt the throw.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep an inside hand extended to "feel" for a stunting interior lineman while keeping your eyes locked on the edge threat.
Depending on the stunt development, be ready to seamlessly pass off the interior defender or catch the looping rusher coming from the outside.
Secure the designated target and drop the anchor, ensuring the depth of the pocket remains entirely intact.
Identify the specific interior assignment (typically a 3-technique defensive tackle) and lock in a balanced pass-blocking stance.
Secure the snap count and execute an aggressive "Angle Set" (a quick 45-degree lateral-forward step to the left) to instantly close the distance to the defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Bending at the Waist. Reaching forward and bending at the waist completely shifts your weight off your anchor. This makes you highly susceptible to "push-pull" or "swim" moves, allowing the defender to effortlessly throw you face-first into the turf.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the spine completely straight and the chest up as you approach contact, refusing to lean forward.
Keep the hands loaded tight to the torso, then deliver a violent, independent hand punch to disrupt the defender's rush path.
Lock out the arms, sink the hips, and continuously mirror the defender to deny any inside or outside counter moves.
Identify the slide direction and mentally lock down the designated gap responsibility (A-gap or B-gap).
On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" to the left directly into the designated slide gap space.
rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Looper. Chasing a defensive lineman who purposefully loops outside completely vacates your assigned zone. This opens up an easy, direct interior lane for an inside stunting lineman to hit the Quarterback untouched.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the upper body perfectly square to the line of scrimmage with hands extended, ready to absorb contact.
Protect the physical gap space itself. Wait for the threat to come to you; do not abandon the zone to chase a looping defender.
Maintain the structural integrity of the interior wall, ensuring no stunting lineman can exploit the interior lane.
Identify your blocking partner (either the Center or Left Tackle) and target the designated interior defensive lineman, noting the second-level linebacker's alignment.
On the snap, take a heavy lateral power step directly toward your teammate to instantly close any physical space between you.
rows.fault_trigger: Splitting Apart. Stepping too shallow or failing to merge hip-to-hip leaves a physical seam between you and your blocking partner. This allows an aggressive, heavy defensive end to split the double team, breach the wall, and blow up the play in the backfield.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Merge entirely hip-to-hip with your blocking partner. Glue your inside hand securely to your partner's hip or lower back to ensure physical unity.
Drive horizontally off the line of scrimmage as a combined unit. Keep your head up and your outside hand completely free to strike the approaching linebacker.
Once the defensive tackle is rolled backward or secured by your partner, seamlessly detach and absorb the second-level linebacker.
Identify the isolated interior defender and establish a heavily coiled run-blocking stance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot the hands violently upward and directly into the defender's armpits to gain inside control.
Sink the hips heavily upon initial contact, then immediately lift upward to completely break the defender's leverage.
Keep the feet wide and unceasingly active ("run your feet") to generate continuous vertical movement down the field.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bring the trailing left foot along without crossing it over the lead foot. Keep the chest completely facing the line of scrimmage to maintain vision.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align with a tight split next to the Center. Set your right foot forward and stagger your left foot back exactly 4 to 6 inches, so your left toe aligns directly with the mid-foot or instep of your right shoe.

rows.fault_trigger: Squatting Too High. Leaving your hips too high before the snap. Standing too upright strips away your natural leverage.

Keep base wide and hips sunk in a quarter-squat, ensuring the rusher's path remains centered relative to your core frame between the legs.

rows.fault_trigger: Reaching / Clapping. Extending both hands prematurely with wide elbows, stripping away length and balance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain continuous foot movement, sliding laterally or vertically to stay positioned strictly between the quarterback and the rusher.
rows.fault_trigger: "Catching" the Rusher. Freezing feet while waiting for contact, destroying leverage and inviting a severe bull-rush.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align in a 3-point stance with left hand down, left foot staggered back (toe-to-instep), minimal weight on fingers.
Pop cleanly out of the stance, driving off the inside right foot into an explosive 45-degree vertical kick step with the left foot.
rows.fault_trigger: False Stepping. Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place pre-snap, stalling the initial kick step and forcing the tackle to chase from behind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inside foot along the turf to preserve a shoulder-width-plus base, keeping the rusher centered over the outside knee.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing Up Straight. Popping upright out of the stance, raising pad level and erasing lateral redirection capabilities.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot an independent left hand punch to the defender's outside chest/shoulder, using the right hand to catch inside counters.

rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping". Picking up the front foot and dropping it in place before advancing, which ruins the timing of the play and lets the defender strike first.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hips square to the imaginary defender even when stepping at an angle, capturing and framing them perfectly between the knees.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-Reaching. Lunging wildly on a reach block, causing the tackle to lose balance and drop to their knees.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot the hands violently straight up into the armpits and inside chest, avoiding clapping out wide.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Identify the dual-threat defensive front (e.g., a defensive end and an outside linebacker), noting both the B-gap responsibility and the edge threat.
On the snap, take a controlled pass set backward and slightly outward, keeping the weight heavily distributed on the inside insteps to allow for instant redirection.
rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Decoy. Aggressively kick-sliding outward to chase a defensive end who is purposely rushing wide to act as a decoy. This completely vacates the B-gap, leaving a massive, unblockable lane for a stunting linebacker to shoot through and violently hit the quarterback from the blindside.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the inside arm engaged or extended to "feel" for a defensive end crashing the B-gap, while locking your eyes on the looping edge threat.
As the stunt develops, seamlessly pass off the crashing inside defender to the Left Guard and firmly redirect your momentum outward to intercept the looping edge rusher.
Secure the new target, drop the hips to anchor, and steer the defender safely past the depth of the quarterback's drop.
Identify the specific edge rusher (often a wide 5-technique or 9-technique) and lock in a staggered, coiled pass-blocking stance.
On the snap, execute an explosive backward "kick step" with the outside (left) foot to instantly gain depth and widen the pocket.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-Setting (Opening the Gate). Kicking backward too deeply and turning your shoulders entirely toward the sideline too early. This "opens the gate," handing the elite edge rusher a direct, unimpeded path to execute an inside counter move (like a spin or rip) straight into the Quarterback's lap.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a completely straight spine with the chest up, dragging the inside (right) foot smoothly to protect the critical inside lane.
Wait for the rusher to enter the physical strike zone, then deliver a violent, independent hand punch to halt their forward momentum.
Lock out the arms, sink the hips, and continuously kick-slide to mirror the defender, steering them harmlessly wide and past the depth of the pocket.
Identify the slide direction and mentally lock down the designated gap responsibility on the left side of the formation.
On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" into the designated slide gap space to immediately seal the lane.
rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Ghost. Drifting outside of your designated zone to chase a wide-rushing defensive end. In a slide protection, this entirely defeats the purpose of the scheme, tearing open a massive B-gap lane for an interior stunting tackle to hit the Quarterback immediately.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the upper body perfectly square to the line of scrimmage with hands extended, ready to absorb any threat entering your cylinder.

Maintain the structural integrity of the offensive line's perimeter, ensuring no stunting lineman can exploit the seam between you and the Left Guard.
Identify your blocking partner (Left Guard or Tight End) and target the designated defensive lineman, noting the second-level linebacker's alignment.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Merge entirely hip-to-hip with your blocking partner. Glue your inside hand securely to your partner's hip or lower back to ensure physical unity.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.
rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)
rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.
rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.
rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the shotgun, reach the mesh maintaining proper spacing to the line of scrimmage, keeping the ball flat and secure and creating a prolonged mesh window (the ball riding from the catch back toward the hip) while holding body position and balance. (Camera judges the QB's own spacing, ball carriage relative to his body, and reach; the exchange itself needs the RB.)
rows.fault_trigger: Collapsing the mesh window, poor spacing or body position, or the ball not kept flat and secure into the mesh. (The running back securing the exchange needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | GUN] Maintain LOS spacing, ball flat + secure catch-to-hip for a prolonged mesh window, hold body position/balance. PROXY (solo) = spacing, ball-vs-body carriage, reach; the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the shotgun snap — aligned roughly 5 yards behind the center in an athletic, slightly-staggered base with the hands up, catching the ball thrown through the air (not a butt-to-gut exchange) — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled catch, hands not presented up, or an unbalanced entry into the exchange. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking; ~5 yards is a recommendation, not a threshold.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | GUN] ~5 yds behind center, athletic slightly-staggered base, hands up to catch a thrown snap (not butt-to-gut); timing/rhythm, balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Chest remains upright, hips loaded, and spine neutral while maintaining an athletic receiving posture.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor receiving posture.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Chest upright, hips loaded, spine neutral — athletic receiving posture. Pad level + posture measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes track the anticipated snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.
rows.fault_trigger: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye tracking not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral while eyes track the anticipated snap location + defensive alignment. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE tracking = deferred. Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center while maintaining posture that allows the snap to enter the center of the receiving window without reaching or drifting.
rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep behind center, forcing a reach or drift for the snap. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] SHOTGUN depth: align at the prescribed depth behind center so the snap enters the center of the receiving window without reaching or drifting. Gun-specific row (under-center has no depth). Relative depth/alignment measurable; absolute needs a scale reference. Partial.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight balanced through mid-foot + balls of the feet for efficient reception without unnecessary body movement. Weight = proxy (ankle-over-mid-foot + stillness is the signal). Partial.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Balanced athletic base supporting clean shotgun reception + immediate movement after the catch. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — lower-body readiness immediately after the catch. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet aligned to support balance during the catch + efficient transition into the play. Foot alignment measurable. Size-independent.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet under the body during the transition — no reaching or excessive movement that disrupts accuracy. A 1 Step drop contains NO crossover. Foot placement measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Strong first step initiating depth while maintaining balance + throwing posture. First-step drive measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

This signal checks squareness only, not depth.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap cleanly. Take an immediate, wide open-gate pivot step at a 90-degree angle toward your rollout side, instantly clearing your frame from the center-exchange space.
rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly on the open-gate pivot that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a wide ~90-degree open-gate pivot, clearing the frame from the center-exchange space instantly. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bring the ball tightly to your chest with both hands, drop your chin, and sprint horizontally at 100% velocity. Because there is no playaction fake, your only protection is outrunning the unblocked edge defender.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Sprint intensity proxy: horizontal (lateral) displacement of Pelvis Center per frame, tracked continuously through the sprint. Coaching target: sustained high displacement-per-frame with no deceleration, consistent with '100% sprint velocity.' NOTE: this reports a RELATIVE displacement rate only - an absolute speed figure needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) and a known frame rate; until then only relative comparisons (e.g. against this player's own top-speed baseline) are meaningful, not a universal threshold. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: As you clear the tackle box, slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This compact step serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Point the Toe. Planting with your foot still pointed wide of the target path. You will slip, blow out your base, or delay your break, resulting in an inaccurate, off-balance throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first to locate your targets. Square your shoulders to your throw, snap your wrist, and deliver the ball while moving downhill to maximize pass velocity.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align tightly 3 to 4 yards deep directly behind the center, with the running back stacked directly behind you. Establish a balanced, shoulder-width parallel stance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line and hip-line should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, confirming a square, symmetric stance. NOTE: the stated alignment depth (e.g. 4.5-5 yards for Gun, 3-4 yards for Pistol) is NOT measurable from pose alone - it requires a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) or field-marking calibration. This signal checks squareness only, not depth.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Catch the snap and immediately execute a fast reverse-pivot to turn your back to the line of scrimmage, generating a linear downhill path for the stacked running back.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a fast ~180-degree reverse-pivot, turning the back toward the line of scrimmage to generate a linear track for the running back. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stick the ball deep into the stomach of the running back as they charge directly downhill. Keep your head and eyes locked into the mesh, shielding the ball with your upper torso to sell a heavy interior run play.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing Too Upright. Failing to bend at the waist during the linear handoff fake. Standing straight up exposes the empty ball to the linebackers, giving away the bootleg instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso flexion: angle between the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line and vertical, measured at the peak of the mesh point (side view). Coaching target: a clear forward bend at the waist, shielding the ball with the upper torso. NOTE: this measures torso BEND only, not 'vision committed to the mesh' - eye gaze is not pose-measurable, and head orientation is not a reliable substitute here since a bent-forward head position is ambiguous between watching the mesh and simply looking down. The coaching standard's real intent (linebackers can't read the fake) is only partially captured by this signal.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slip the ball out of the mesh late. Slam your outside foot down hard under your hips with the toe pulled up into sharp dorsiflexion. Instantly point your toe toward the perimeter to drive your body weight out of the linear track and onto a wide, looping rollout line.
rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding the Plant. Reaching too far forward to change direction out of the linear track. This locks up your hips and prevents you from getting your shoulders squared up to make an accurate throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first. Keep your front shoulder tucked, square your chest to the line of throw, and unleash the football with full velocity while clearing the edge.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand secures the front — ball tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low or away from the torso approaching the exchange. (Ball position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure the ball with two hands — throwing hand back half, off-hand front half — tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; ball position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)
rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.
rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate eye discipline based on the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange mechanics.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes tip the play or disrupt the exchange. (Eye gaze/discipline not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Appropriate eye discipline for the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange / tipping the play. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/discipline = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use a tight two-step footwork pattern (for example opening at roughly 45° into the A-gap) to clear entirely off the center-to-tailback straight line, aligning the toes parallel to the running back's incoming track — controlled, downhill-connected steps with proper spacing, timing and balance.
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to clear the center-to-tailback line, a loose or wide pattern instead of the tight two-step, or toes not aligned to the back's track. (The 45° / A-gap opening is illustrative of clearing the midline, not a fixed threshold; the aiming point depends on the run concept, which is not captured — reported, not judged.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS MOTION | PISTOL] Tight two-step pattern (e.g. ~45° into the A-gap, illustrative not a threshold) to clear the center-to-tailback line; toes parallel to the RB's track; controlled downhill steps. Step/open-angle + track measurable; aiming point (run concept) deferred — report, don't judge.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the pistol snap — aligned closer to the line (roughly 3 yards) in an upright posture to survey the defense, catching the ball cleanly and preparing for the downhill mesh — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled catch, or an unbalanced entry that isn't ready for the downhill mesh. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking; ~3 yards is a recommendation, not a threshold.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | PISTOL] ~3 yds, upright to survey; clean catch preparing for the downhill mesh; timing/rhythm, balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the pistol alignment (closer to the line, roughly 3 yards, upright to survey the defense), maintain the correct depth relationship so the exchange with the deeper-aligned tailback keeps its timing, spacing, and blocking angles.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong pistol depth relationship, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (~3 yards is a recommendation, not a calibrated threshold; absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative | PISTOL] Pistol ~3 yds, upright — maintain the depth relationship so the deeper-aligned tailback's exchange keeps timing/spacing/blocking angles. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale (~3 yds is a recommendation, not a threshold).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.
rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the pistol, reach a downhill mesh on a balanced base with the ball seated near the back hip/belly and soft, pressure-ready hands, letting the deeper-aligned tailback press straight through the mesh point. (Camera judges the QB's downhill track, base, and ball position relative to his body; the exchange itself needs the RB.)
rows.fault_trigger: Losing the downhill track or the balanced base, or the ball not seated for the deeper tailback's straight path through the mesh. (The running back securing the exchange needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | PISTOL] Downhill mesh, balanced base, ball seated near the back hip/belly with soft pressure-ready hands for the deeper tailback's straight path. PROXY (solo) = downhill track, base, ball-vs-body position; the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.
rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes focus on the expected snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.
rows.fault_trigger: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral while eyes focus on the expected snap location + defensive alignment. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE focus = deferred. Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center to ensure the football enters the optimal receiving window and preserves offensive timing.
rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep behind center, hurting the window or timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] PISTOL depth: align at the prescribed depth behind center so the ball enters the optimal receiving window + preserves offensive timing. Pistol depth is SHORTER than shotgun (~3-3.5 yds vs ~5). Relative depth/alignment measurable; absolute needs a scale reference. Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight remains balanced through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, supporting efficient reception and downhill movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight on the heels — delays downhill movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight balanced through mid-foot + balls of the feet for efficient reception + downhill movement. Weight = proxy (ankle-over-mid-foot is the signal). Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hands positioned comfortably in front of the torso at the anticipated snap location — fingers naturally spread and relaxed with elbows slightly flexed, creating a consistent receiving window that cushions the football into secure two-hand possession.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands off the window, stiff, or poor finger spread. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
pose_landmarks: Right Elbow. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] PISTOL receiving window: hands comfortably in front of the torso at the anticipated snap location; fingers naturally spread + relaxed, elbows slightly flexed, a consistent window cushioning the ball into secure two-hand possession. Hand POSITION = pose-measurable; FINGER detail = needs the Hand landmarker. Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet maintain proper stagger, toe angle, and alignment for balanced snap reception and efficient first movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong stagger/toe angle — unstable reception or inefficient first movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Proper stagger, toe angle, alignment — balanced snap reception + efficient first movement. Foot stagger/angle measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed to maintain an explosive athletic posture while preparing for the snap.
rows.fault_trigger: Knees locked or over-bent — loses explosive readiness.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knees slightly flexed — explosive athletic posture while preparing for the snap. Knee angle measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet establish an athletic base supporting downhill movement immediately following snap reception.
rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide for balanced downhill movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Athletic base supporting downhill movement immediately following snap reception. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain loaded hips, controlled chest, and neutral spine to support both downhill run action and passing mechanics.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor support for run/pass.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Loaded hips, controlled chest, neutral spine — supports both downhill run action + passing mechanics. Pad level + posture measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain square to the line of scrimmage while supporting efficient transition into the offensive concept.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders not square to the LOS.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders square to the LOS — efficient transition into the offensive concept. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso, allowing immediate power generation after the catch.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — immediate power generation after the catch. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the fake into the designed pass footwork with efficient steps — feet under the body, maintaining balance, rhythm, and timing.
rows.fault_trigger: Wasted/choppy steps or feet out from under the body transitioning into the pass phase.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition from the fake into the pass footwork with efficient steps — feet under the body, throwing rhythm/balance/timing maintained. Footwork efficiency + step detection measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand security during the fake and transition — the ball remains protected against the body until the QB commits to the throw.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball exposed or dropped to one hand during the fake/transition. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand security through the fake and transition; ball protected against the body until committing to the throw (cross-cutting Ball Security). POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver the football on schedule based on the route concept and defensive reaction while maintaining rhythm from fake to throw.
rows.fault_trigger: Late/early or arrhythmic delivery from fake to throw. (On-schedule-for-route/defense judgment needs the route + defense; ball flight needs ball tracking — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Deliver on schedule per the route concept + defensive reaction, keeping rhythm from fake to throw. The QB's release TIMING/rhythm (fake→throw) is measurable from body motion; but 'on schedule for the route/defense' depends on the ROUTE + DEFENSE not in a solo clip — that judgment is deferred. Ball flight needs ball tracking. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use the eyes to influence defenders during the fake, then quickly transition vision to the defensive read and receiver progression while maintaining body control.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes give away the fake or fail to transition to the read. (Eye gaze/reads not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Use eyes to influence defenders during the fake, then transition vision to the read/receiver progression while keeping body control. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/reads = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sell the run by committing the entire body — eyes, shoulders, hips, and ball presentation replicate the intended run concept; avoid pulling the ball early, creating a believable run picture before transitioning to throw.
rows.fault_trigger: Half-hearted body commitment or pulling the ball early — no believable run picture. (Ball-presentation + eye parts need ball tracking / are gaze-deferred.)
pose_landmarks: Sternum. (Ball Position needs ball tracking; eyes = gaze deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Sell the run with full-body commitment — eyes, shoulders, hips, ball presentation replicate the run concept; don't pull the ball early; create a believable run picture. Pistol = downhill full-body sell. BODY sell (shoulder/hip/posture + not-pulling-early timing) = measurable; BALL presentation = needs BALL TRACKING; eyes/gaze = deferred. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain controlled shoulders through the fake, then rotate efficiently toward the target without opening early.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or over-rotate through the fake, hurting accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled shoulders through the fake, then rotate efficiently toward the target without opening early (which hurts accuracy). Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the snap with proper timing and rhythm from cadence — body balanced — and transition smoothly into the designed play-action footwork.
rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed/bobbled snap or unbalanced/slow transition into the play-action footwork. (Finger/ball detail needs hand model / ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Right Knee. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — folded-in note] Snap received with proper timing/rhythm from cadence, body balanced, transitions smoothly into play-action footwork. Under center = hands under center; gun/pistol = clean catch (pistol prepares for downhill). Snap detail also folded into Stance. Timing/balance/transition measurable; finger + ball detail needs hand model / ball tracking. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips controlled during the fake, then rotate efficiently through the throw to generate power and maintain accuracy.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips over-open early or fail to rotate through the throw, losing power/accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips controlled during the fake, then rotate efficiently through the throw for power + accuracy (pistol: keep hips underneath the body). Hip-line + rotation timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Regain a balanced throwing posture with feet underneath the body, hips loaded, knees slightly bent, and shoulders ready to align toward the target.
rows.fault_trigger: Fails to reset into a loaded, aligned, throwing-ready posture after the fake.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Regain a throwing-ready posture — knees slightly bent, hips loaded, feet under the body, shoulders ready to align to the target. The reset-to-throw state (base + load + alignment) measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain proper depth from the line of scrimmage after the snap and fake — depth creates throwing lanes while preserving route timing.
rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow (no lane) or too deep/drifting after the fake, breaking timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] Maintain proper depth from the LOS after snap + fake (pistol: relationship from center + backfield action) — depth creates throwing lanes while preserving route timing. Relative depth/position measurable; absolute needs a scale. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands at chest level — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand protects the front — ball tight to the body frame with elbows close until the mesh action begins.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low, elbows flared, or away from the body before the mesh. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two hands at chest level — throwing hand back half, off-hand front — ball tight to the body frame, elbows close, until the mesh begins. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the fake at correct depth, timing, and spacing with the RB — present the ball into the exchange window with both hands, extend to sell the run, hold the mesh long enough to influence defenders, then retract smoothly into a secure throwing position.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong mesh depth/timing/spacing, weak extension, or rushed retraction. (Mesh quality needs the RB + ball — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Right Foot. (Mesh quality needs the RB + Ball Position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — mostly DEFERRED, 2-PERSON + BALL] Fake at correct depth/timing/spacing with the RB: present the ball into the exchange window with both hands, extend to sell the run, hold the mesh to influence defenders, then retract smoothly into a secure throwing position. Pistol = downhill exchange point. Mirrors Hand Off Mesh Point (difference: here the QB PULLS + throws). HEAVILY 2-person + ball. PROXY (solo) = QB's extend-retract arm motion + footwork/position. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced base with proper foot placement, weight transfer, and shoulder/hip alignment before release.
rows.fault_trigger: Narrow/wide base, poor weight transfer, or misaligned shoulders/hips before release.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Balanced base — proper foot placement, weight transfer, shoulder/hip alignment — before release. The throwing platform (base + transfer + alignment) measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use short, controlled steps while maintaining a balanced base — feet remain underneath the body and avoid crossing.
rows.fault_trigger: Long/uncontrolled steps or crossing the feet, losing balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Short, controlled steps, balanced base, feet under the body, no crossing. Step size + crossing detection measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Climb forward through the pocket with minimal lateral drift, preserving throwing lanes and relationship with the offensive-line structure.
rows.fault_trigger: Excessive lateral drift instead of a forward climb.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Climb FORWARD with minimal lateral drift, preserving lanes. Forward path + lateral-drift measurable (direction/path) from pose. (OL relationship implies linemen not in a solo clip.) FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Protect the football with two hands while climbing — ball remains tight to the torso until the throwing decision is made.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball drops to one hand or away from the torso while climbing. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two hands protect the ball while climbing, tight to torso until the throw decision. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Recognize pressure location and identify available space before movement begins — movement is intentional and creates a cleaner throwing lane.
rows.fault_trigger: Late/unintentional movement or moving into pressure. (Pressure recognition itself not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Recognize pressure location + identify space before moving; movement intentional, creating a cleaner lane. Pressure recognition = perception (implies a rusher not in a solo clip), NOT directly measurable; PROXY = the resulting intentional movement + head up. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep eyes downfield while moving — head remains stable and independent from lower-body movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Head drops or bobs with the lower body. (Actual gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Eyes downfield while moving; head stable + independent from lower body. Head STABILITY/orientation measurable; actual GAZE deferred. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a functional throwing base during movement — feet separated enough to absorb contact and redirect.
rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow to absorb contact or redirect while climbing.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Functional throwing base during movement — feet separated enough to absorb contact + redirect. Base width (ankle distance) measurable, size-independent. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
