rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Reach the proper seven-step depth with balanced throwing posture — protection space while preserving timing with deeper routes. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the longer drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. Base stays wide enough to hold balance.
rows.fault_trigger: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Toes pointing backward. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Wasted steps or excessive vertical movement in the deeper drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet glide low to the ground through the longer drop — low vertical oscillation of the ankles/hips, ground contact maintained, no wasted steps. The THREE designed crossovers are foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a strong drive step that initiates depth while maintaining balance and protecting the throwing posture.
rows.fault_trigger: Weak drive step or lost balance/posture initiating the deeper drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Strong DRIVE step initiating depth while keeping balance + protecting throwing posture. First/drive-step measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and controlled through the longer drop — avoiding early opening while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulders stay level and controlled through the drop. The front shoulder neither collapses nor over-rotates — either turns the hips prematurely and blinds vision to one side.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or tilt during the deeper drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + controlled through the longer drop — avoid opening early while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set up in a balanced, parallel stance under center, keeping your weight perfectly symmetrical and your hands pressed tightly into the exchange pocket.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) and hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, with no lateral tilt or rotation - confirming a square, symmetric base under center. NOTE: this checks squareness only; it cannot confirm true weight distribution (a separate Draft proxy elsewhere), and proximity to the snap exchange is not measurable without the Center in frame.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute an immediate open-gate pivot (opening your hips 90 degrees directly toward your rollout path) and take a violent, deep escape stride sideways.
rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a sharp ~90-degree open-gate pivot, opening the hips directly toward the rollout path. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Because there is no ball fake, the deception is pure speed. Bring the ball tightly to your chest with both hands, drop your chin, and sprint horizontally at 100% velocity to outrun the unblocked edge defender.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Sprint intensity proxy: horizontal (lateral) displacement of Pelvis Center per frame, tracked continuously through the sprint. Coaching target: sustained high displacement-per-frame with no deceleration, consistent with '100% sprint velocity.' NOTE: this reports a RELATIVE displacement rate only - an absolute speed figure needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) and a known frame rate; until then only relative comparisons (e.g. against this player's own top-speed baseline) are meaningful, not a universal threshold. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: As you reach a depth of 6-7 yards deep in the backfield, slam your outside foot into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This foot serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Direct the Foot. Planting with your toe still pointed toward your deep drop track. This causes you to drift endlessly toward the sideline, completely shrinking your throwing window and running out of bounds.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first to locate your targets. Square your shoulders to your throw, snap your wrist, and deliver the ball while moving downhill to maximize pass velocity.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a perfectly square, parallel base under the center. Ride your hands securely under the center's hips with your weight evenly distributed on the balls of your feet.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) and hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, with no lateral tilt or rotation - confirming a square, symmetric base under center. NOTE: this checks squareness only; it cannot confirm true weight distribution (a separate Draft proxy elsewhere), and proximity to the snap exchange is not measurable without the Center in frame.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the ball and execute a violent reverse-pivot off your lead foot. Take an aggressive, deep crossover drop step away from the line of scrimmage, pointing your back toward the line to start your track toward the fake running back.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a violent ~180-degree reverse-pivot, turning the back toward the line of scrimmage. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Seat the ball deeply into the running back's belly pocket with both hands. Ensure your head and eyes snap completely down into the fake mesh point, bending your waist slightly to shield the ball with your upper torso from the eyes of the linebackers.
rows.fault_trigger: Staring Downfield. Keeping your eyes up and looking downfield during the mesh. If you don't commit your vision and head to the fake handoff, the linebackers will never bite on the run.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso flexion: angle between the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line and vertical, measured at the peak of the mesh point (side view). Coaching target: a clear forward bend at the waist, shielding the ball with the upper torso. NOTE: this measures torso BEND only, not 'vision committed to the mesh' - eye gaze is not pose-measurable, and head orientation is not a reliable substitute here since a bent-forward head position is ambiguous between watching the mesh and simply looking down. The coaching standard's real intent (linebackers can't read the fake) is only partially captured by this signal.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Rip the ball out of the mesh at the last millisecond. Slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe and directing your final step down a wide, looping track toward the opposite edge. Hide the ball tightly against your back hip as you clear the edge.
rows.fault_trigger: Rounding the Corner. Drifting too deep or running a lazy, wide circle into the backfield. Failing to point your foot and drive flat along the edge allows an unblocked defensive end to hunt you down for a loss.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield to locate the target. Square your shoulders completely to the target, keep your front shoulder pointed down the field, and deliver an accurate pass while maintaining forward-running momentum.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'

rows.ideal_execution_standard: After securing the snap (ball 'butt to gut' — both hands to the stomach/chest before any movement), pivot and open toward the direction of the run and step along the designated track that matches the running back's path — efficient steps, proper spacing, timing and balance, staying on the track — with the eyes up on the read key / defensive line and peripheral vision guiding the exchange. The toes point along the designated track for the called run (the aiming point varies by run concept).
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to open toward the run, stepping off the designated track, or crossing/choppy steps that stop momentum or drift off the path. (The track's aiming point depends on the called run concept, which is not captured — the app reports the track / open angle but does not judge which is correct.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS MOTION | UNDER CENTER] Secure 'butt to gut', pivot/open toward the run, step on the designated track matching the RB path; eyes up on the read key. Footwork efficiency + open angle/track measurable from pose; the aiming point depends on the run concept (deferred) — report the track, don't judge it.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)
rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Under center, the exchange happens at the mesh right off the line of scrimmage, so depth is not the governing relationship — hold the designated track and mesh position (rather than a fixed backfield depth) so timing, spacing, and blocking angles are preserved.
rows.fault_trigger: Drifting off the designated track or mesh position, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (Under center the handoff is at the mesh, not depth-based; absolute distance needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY | UNDER CENTER] Under center the exchange is at the mesh off the LOS, not depth-based — hold the designated track + mesh position for timing/spacing/blocking angles. Relative track/position measurable from pose; absolute distance needs a scale reference.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate eye discipline based on the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange mechanics.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes tip the play or disrupt the exchange. (Eye gaze/discipline not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Appropriate eye discipline for the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange / tipping the play. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/discipline = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand secures the front — ball tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low or away from the torso approaching the exchange. (Ball position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure the ball with two hands — throwing hand back half, off-hand front half — tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; ball position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the designed mesh point right off the line of scrimmage on the correct track, presenting the ball with both hands into the running path while keeping body position and balance. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own track, reach, and ball position relative to his body; whether the running back secures the exchange needs the RB in frame.)
rows.fault_trigger: An off-track approach to the mesh, poor body position or balance, or the ball not presented into the running path. (Mesh quality itself — the running back securing the ball — needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | UNDER CENTER] Off the LOS, reach the mesh on the correct track; present the ball into the running path; keep body position/balance. PROXY (solo) = the QB's own track, reach motion, ball-vs-body position; the RB securing the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.
rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.
rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.
rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the snap from under center — hands seated under the center, the ball delivered 'butt to gut' and immediately secured with both hands to the stomach/chest — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.
rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled snap, hands not seated under center, or an unbalanced entry into the exchange. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | UNDER CENTER] Hands under center, ball 'butt to gut' secured immediately; timing/rhythm, body balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable from pose; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded with the chest upright and spine neutral — the body remains compact and balanced while preparing to receive the snap.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — not compact/balanced for the snap.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips loaded, chest upright, spine neutral — body compact + balanced preparing to receive the snap. Pad level (how loaded/low) + posture measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet are staggered so the NON-THROWING-side foot sits slightly back — left foot back for a right-handed QB, right foot back for a left-handed QB. The stagger loads the back leg, lets the QB push off efficiently, and starts the drop without a false step forward. Feet stay roughly shoulder-width apart (about armpit width) with knees comfortably flexed and a stable toe-to-heel relationship and toe angle. NOTE: the stagger direction depends on the player's throwing hand — handedness must be supplied by the app before this can be judged; without it, report the observed stagger without scoring it.
rows.fault_trigger: Feet square with no stagger, or the THROWING-side foot back instead of the non-throwing side — the back leg cannot load and the QB takes a false step forward to start the drop. Stagger too deep or too shallow to push off cleanly, or toe angle creating an unstable platform. (Judging which foot should be back requires the player's handedness.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Proper toe-to-heel relationship, stagger, and angle — stable exchange platform + efficient first step. Foot stagger/angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.coaching_cue: Non-throwing foot back — load it, don't false step.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and square to the line of scrimmage and center, allowing a controlled snap exchange and efficient transition into the play.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders tilted or not square to the LOS/center.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + square to the LOS/center — controlled snap exchange + efficient transition. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight centered through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, allowing explosive movement immediately after the snap without rocking forward or backward.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight on the heels or rocking forward/backward, delaying movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight centered through the mid-foot + balls of the feet for explosive post-snap movement, no rocking forward/backward. Weight = proxy (pose can't measure force; ankle-over-mid-foot + no rocking is the signal). Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bottom hand directly beneath the center with palm facing upward, top hand covering — fingers naturally spread and relaxed for a broad receiving target, wrists relaxed and elbows close to cushion the snap and immediately secure the football.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands not seated under center, poor palm/finger relationship, or elbows flared — muffed/insecure snap. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
pose_landmarks: Right Elbow. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] UNDER CENTER hand placement: bottom hand directly beneath center, palm UP, top hand covering; fingers naturally spread + relaxed for a broad target; wrists relaxed, elbows close to cushion the snap + immediately secure the ball. Hand POSITION (wrist/elbow) = pose-measurable; FINGER spread/palm detail = needs the Hand landmarker. THIS is the key under-center-specific row (differs from shotgun window). Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet approximately shoulder-width apart — roughly under the armpits — establishing a balanced athletic base that supports efficient snap reception and immediate movement after the exchange, with knees comfortably flexed and weight balanced on the balls of the feet.
rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow or too wide for a balanced exchange platform.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet ~shoulder-width apart — balanced athletic base supporting efficient snap reception + immediate movement. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso, allowing efficient force transfer immediately following the snap.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips rotated/off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — efficient force transfer following the snap. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral with the chin level — eyes maintain disciplined pre-snap focus while preserving proper body posture and awareness.
rows.fault_trigger: Head tilted/dropped or chin not level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral, chin level; disciplined pre-snap focus while preserving posture + awareness. Head ORIENTATION/level measurable; actual EYE focus = deferred. Partial.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed, creating an athletic posture that supports a stable exchange and efficient movement after possession.
rows.fault_trigger: Knees locked straight or over-bent — loses athletic readiness.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knees slightly flexed — athletic posture supporting a stable exchange + efficient movement. Knee angle measurable. Size-independent.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Assume a balanced stance with the right foot staggered back slightly to allow an explosive forward-diagonal angle set to the right.
Fire the right foot diagonally on an aggressive angle set to close space on a 3-technique tackle, keeping the base strictly wide.
Drag the left foot to replace the base without narrowing, keeping the defender centered between the knees and shoulders square.
Explode the right hand out first as the primary strike into the chest, anchoring the left hand inside the opposite pectoral to stun momentum.
rows.fault_trigger: Flaring Elbows. Allowing elbows to swing outward, exposing the guard's own chest plate to easy control.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the feet pattering in micro-steps backward to absorb any power transition, anchoring the front-side pocket wall.
rows.fault_trigger: Lunging & Over-Extending. Shifting weight onto the toes, which locks the knees, stops foot movement, and lets the rusher easily pull the guard forward.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Adopt a rigid, loaded 3-point stance with the right foot staggered back. Weight is balanced 60% forward and 40% back to optimize forward launch.
Explode forward to execute heavy base blocks to drive 3-techniques outward or down blocks to collapse the line.
Deliver high-knee, powerful driving steps, keeping your midsection directly aligned with the center mass of the imaginary threat.
rows.fault_trigger: Waist Bending. Bending over at the waist instead of hinging at the knees and hips, killing all leg-drive leverage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode both hands into the inside chest frame/armpits, clamping down on jersey cloth while keeping elbows tightly squeezed against the ribs.
rows.fault_trigger: Elbow Flaring. Letting the elbows flare out on contact, which diminishes power and allows the defensive tackle to slide right off the block.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a rapid, continuous foot-patter, keeping the drive forward with short, choppy bursts until the whistle blows.

Set a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your left foot forward. Keep your chest and shoulders perfectly parallel to the ball line, masking whether you are dropping into pass protection or executing a run pull.
Stagger your right foot back exactly 3 to 4 inches, aligning your right toe strictly with the mid-foot arch of your left shoe.
rows.fault_trigger: Deep Heel Stagger. Dropping the right foot 10+ inches back. A deep stagger in a gun alignment opens up your inside B-gap, inviting interior defensive tackles to shoot the gap for an instant sack.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: right foot staggered back a moderate, visible amount (3-4in). NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower your hips and shift your center of gravity backward, establishing a balanced 45% forward / 55% backward weight split to prioritize pass protection drop speed.
Drop your right hand down to the grass, placing only your fingertips on the turf with virtually zero weight on them. Tuck your left hand close to your left thigh in a ready state.
rows.fault_trigger: Heavy Hand Pressure. Placing heavy physical weight onto your down hand. If you lean forward, you cannot execute a flat lateral pull or a clean vertical pass set.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lock your framework into a compressed coil. Keep your core braced and your heels lightly kissing the grass, ready to instantly slide or punch.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set a wide 12-to-18-inch split from the Center, placing your left foot forward. Keep your chest and shoulders perfectly parallel to the ball line, masking whether you are dropping into pass protection or executing a run pull.
Stagger your right foot back exactly 3 to 4 inches, aligning your right toe strictly with the mid-foot arch of your left shoe.
rows.fault_trigger: Deep Heel Stagger. Dropping the right foot 10+ inches back. A deep stagger in a gun alignment opens up your inside B-gap, inviting interior defensive tackles to shoot the gap for an instant sack.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: right foot staggered back a moderate, visible amount (3-4in). NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower your hips and shift your center of gravity backward, establishing a balanced 45% forward / 55% backward weight split to prioritize pass protection drop speed.
Drop your right hand down to the grass, placing only your fingertips on the turf with virtually zero weight on them. Tuck your left hand close to your left thigh in a ready state.
rows.fault_trigger: Heavy Hand Pressure. Placing heavy physical weight onto your down hand. If you lean forward, you cannot execute a flat lateral pull or a clean vertical pass set.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lock your framework into a compressed coil. Keep your core braced and your heels lightly kissing the grass, ready to instantly slide or punch.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Identify the dual-threat defensive front, noting both the immediate interior gap responsibility and the potential outside looping threat.
On the snap, set at a controlled 45-degree angle to the right, keeping a perfectly balanced weight distribution on the balls of the feet.
rows.fault_trigger: Dropping Too Deep. Dropping too deep backward in the pass set abandons the line of scrimmage. This forces the pocket to shrink vertically, allowing the defensive line to easily compress the space around the quarterback and disrupt the throw.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep an inside hand extended to "feel" for a stunting interior lineman while keeping your eyes locked on the edge threat.
Depending on the stunt development, be ready to seamlessly pass off the interior defender or catch the looping rusher coming from the outside.
Secure the designated target and drop the anchor, ensuring the depth of the pocket remains entirely intact.
Identify the specific interior assignment (typically a 3-technique defensive tackle) and lock in a balanced pass-blocking stance.
Secure the snap count and execute an aggressive "Angle Set" (a quick 45-degree lateral-forward step to the right) to instantly close the distance to the defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Bending at the Waist. Reaching forward and bending at the waist completely shifts your weight off your anchor. This makes you highly susceptible to "push-pull" or "swim" moves, allowing the defender to effortlessly throw you face-first into the turf.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the spine completely straight and the chest up as you approach contact, refusing to lean forward.
Keep the hands loaded tight to the torso, then deliver a violent, independent hand punch to disrupt the defender's rush path.
Lock out the arms, sink the hips, and continuously mirror the defender to deny any inside or outside counter moves.
Identify the slide direction and mentally lock down the designated gap responsibility (A-gap or B-gap).
On the snap, take a lateral "catch step" to the right directly into the designated slide gap space.
rows.fault_trigger: Chasing the Looper. Chasing a defensive lineman who purposefully loops outside completely vacates your assigned zone. This opens up an easy, direct interior lane for an inside stunting lineman to hit the Quarterback untouched.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the upper body perfectly square to the line of scrimmage with hands extended, ready to absorb contact.
Protect the physical gap space itself. Wait for the threat to come to you; do not abandon the zone to chase a looping defender.
Maintain the structural integrity of the interior wall, ensuring no stunting lineman can exploit the interior lane.
Identify your blocking partner (either the Center or Right Tackle) and target the designated interior defensive lineman, noting the second-level linebacker's alignment.
On the snap, take a heavy lateral power step directly toward your teammate to instantly close any physical space between you.
rows.fault_trigger: Splitting Apart. Stepping too shallow or failing to merge hip-to-hip leaves a physical seam between you and your blocking partner. This allows an aggressive, heavy defensive end to split the double team, breach the wall, and blow up the play in the backfield.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Merge entirely hip-to-hip with your blocking partner. Glue your inside hand securely to your partner's hip or lower back to ensure physical unity.
Drive horizontally off the line of scrimmage as a combined unit. Keep your head up and your outside hand completely free to strike the approaching linebacker.
Once the defensive tackle is rolled backward or secured by your partner, seamlessly detach and absorb the second-level linebacker.
Identify the isolated interior defender and establish a heavily coiled run-blocking stance.
On the snap, explode forward out of the stance with a powerful displacement step to instantly close the cushion.
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Bring the Hips Through. Hitting the defender without rolling your hips through the contact results in a weak, top-heavy block. Relying entirely on upper-body strength guarantees you will lose leverage and get shed.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoot the hands violently upward and directly into the defender's armpits to gain inside control.
Sink the hips heavily upon initial contact, then immediately lift upward to completely break the defender's leverage.
Keep the feet wide and unceasingly active ("run your feet") to generate continuous vertical movement down the field.
Identify the designated pull direction (to the left), the intended insertion hole, and the target linebacker assignment.
On the snap, open immediately with a short lateral slide step to the left.
rows.fault_trigger: Crossing the Feet. Crossing the trailing foot over the lead foot during the skip completely destroys your base. It guarantees you will trip over your own feet or immediately lose your balance and get knocked over upon hitting a defender.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bring the trailing right foot along without crossing it over the lead foot. Keep the chest completely facing the line of scrimmage to maintain vision.
Keep your eyes up-field, locate the target linebacker, and violently burst forward into the designated hole.
Make decisive contact with the second-level defender, driving your momentum entirely through their frame to clear the lane.
Identify the designated pull path and mentally lock onto the unblocked edge or interior defender slated for the kick-out.
On the snap, take an aggressive, perfectly flat "open step" to the left, pivoting exactly 90 degrees on the left foot.
rows.fault_trigger: Pulling Too Deep. Looping backward into the backfield instead of running a tight line allows the unblocked defender to penetrate too deeply. This ruins the geometry of the play and results in a tackle for loss.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Run a tight, straight line right across the heels of the remaining offensive linemen; do not bow or loop backward into the backfield.
As you close the distance on the penetrating defender, intentionally drop your inside shoulder to establish lower leverage.
Deliver a violent, explosive kick-out block directly into the defender's flank, completely clearing them out of the running lane.

Align with a tight 6-to-12-inch split next to the Center, setting your left foot forward. Square your shoulders perfectly to the line of scrimmage. Do not angle your hips outward, as this alerts the interior defense to an outside running play.
Stagger your right foot back exactly 4 to 6 inches, so your right toe aligns directly with the mid-foot or instep of your left shoe.
rows.fault_trigger: Deep Tackle Stagger. Dropping the right foot 12+ inches back like a tackle. A deep stagger locks up a guard's hips, making it nearly impossible to pull cleanly to the left or make a flat lateral block.

Coaching target: right foot staggered back a large, clearly visible amount (10-12in). NOTE: deliberately weaker than the side-view version of this checkpoint; use side view whenever available.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stagger your right foot back deeply exactly 10 to 12 inches, ensuring your right toe aligns directly behind your left heel to protect your outside edge.
rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Base or Weak Stagger. Setting the stagger at only 4 inches. A shallow tackle stagger allows speed-rushers to instantly clip your outside shoulder before you can get depth in a kick-slide.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Horizontal distance between the rear foot and front foot ground-contact points (Heel/Foot Index, whichever registers lower in the image), resolved in the image plane along the front-to-back axis (perpendicular to the line of scrimmage). Reported in torso-lengths (Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center as the scale unit) since side view cannot see shoulder width for scaling. Coaching target: 10-12 inches. NOTE: absolute-inch conversion needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture - open decision, not yet built); until then this reports a relative torso-length value only, uncalibrated.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drop your weight low. Keep your balance split at 55% forward / 45% backward, ensuring you have enough forward tilt to drive block an exterior edge rusher while maintaining back-foot leverage.
Lower your right hand to the ground, placing it slightly outside your right knee frame. Keep your left hand braced securely against your left thigh to establish a rigid 3-point platform.
rows.fault_trigger: Locked Front Knee. Failing to bend your front knee sufficiently when reaching down. This forces your back to hunch and locks up your legs.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lock your spine flat and look up. Keep your core heavily braced and your lower joints compressed like a high-tension spring, ready to launch forward or kick-slide wide.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso lean angle: the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line angle relative to vertical, tracked from Stance Locking into Coiled Readiness. A stable angle is expected; a sudden late increase suggests the back arching/rounding as weight settles. NOTE: measures overall torso LEAN, not spinal curvature - no mid-back landmark exists in the 33-point model, so true rounding is not directly visible. Flagged Partial for that reason, not Yes.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the catch in space and transition the ball directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field turn before the ball is possessed.
rows.fault_trigger: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or turn up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.
rows.fault_trigger: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.
rows.fault_trigger: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Read interior pursuit and transfer the ball to the outside arm (closest to the sideline), freeing the inside arm to stiff-arm or guard against incoming tacklers.
The moment traffic closes in or a tackle is initiated, wrap the off-hand over the ball (two-handed carry) and chin the football to protect it completely through the ground.

Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.
rows.fault_trigger: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Intercept the nose of the ball out wide in the centre of the diamond, elbows unlocked to absorb the high-velocity lateral momentum. The nose must be pointed exactly at the hands at the moment of impact - not tracking the ball peripherally.
rows.fault_trigger: THE PERIPHERAL PEEK - trying to catch using only peripheral vision with the nose pointed straight downfield, which ruins hand-eye coordination and depth perception. THE STIFF LATERAL LOCKOUT - catching out wide with locked elbows, so the ball clanks off rigid fingertips.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sweep the ball back tightly across the body into the core ribcage, instantly snapping the chin down and across the torso to visually lock the ball into the tuck position before looking upfield.
rows.fault_trigger: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.
rows.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently across the chest, rolling the head diagonally downward to visually track the ball all the way from the high-outside quadrant into chest protection as the feet return to the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.
rows.fault_trigger: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inverted hands underneath the dipping path of the ball, with the chin tucked to the catch-side shoulder and the eyes glued to the grass-level pinky basket as the ball settles in.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes lifting off the basket before the fingers close. On a low-and-wide catch the hands are at their furthest from the head, so peripheral tracking is at its least reliable and the margin is smallest.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.
rows.fault_trigger: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold a strong base with the eyes locked on the point of the ball. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.
rows.fault_trigger: BODY CATCHING - letting the ball travel all the way into the chest pads instead of extending the hands, so it bounces off hard plastic armour and results in drops or deflections. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Let the nose of the ball enter the centre of the diamond while the eyes stay hyper-focused on the leather. The elbows stay relaxed and flexible to give with the ball and absorb its force, with the fingertips - not the palms - clamping the panels.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY LOOK - snapping the head up to look at an oncoming defender right before the ball hits the hands, causing a ricochet off the fingertips. THE STIFF-ARM CLANK - catching with locked-out elbows and hard palms; without joint elasticity a fast ball clanks off the hands. (Ball contact needs object detection.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball tightly back into the ribcage, wrapping the arm completely over it for a four-point pressure hold. Instantly drop the chin to visually confirm the catch - nose to the tuck - before snapping the eyes upfield to look for defenders.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes leaving the ball before the tuck is complete - the head comes up to find defenders while the ball is still being secured, which is how a clean catch becomes a fumble. Also: no chin drop at all, so the catch is never visually confirmed.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high trajectory and time the jump or extension so the hands intercept the ball at the absolute apex of reach. Shoot both arms violently upward above the forehead with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs pressed tightly together and index fingers pointing up, creating an inverted triangle to look through.
rows.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES OUT - reaching up for a high ball with the pinkies together instead of the thumbs. This turns the palms away from the ball and makes a clean high catch impossible. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stare directly through the window created by the hands and pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible point, fingers spread wide and thumbs facing each other right before impact, fingertips wrapping tightly around the tip and sides to halt its momentum mid-air.
rows.fault_trigger: THE BLIND PULL - tilting the head back down toward the turf before the hands secure the ball, resulting in a blind, clapping attempt at the apex. CLAPPING AT THE BALL - slapping the hands together from the sides; if the timing is off by a millisecond the palms hit the ball and knock it away.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently to the chest as the feet return to the turf, the head snapping down to follow the ball's descent from the sky straight into the core, then immediately roll the body or shoulders over the ball to protect it from closing defenders.
rows.fault_trigger: Head staying tilted up after the catch rather than following the ball down into the body, so the tuck is never visually confirmed. Also: landing stiff-legged without knee flexion, costing balance and the ability to run after the catch.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the downward trajectory and lower the entire body frame by bending at the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist. Drop the arms toward the grass with elbows tucked close to the torso, then invert the hands completely - pinky fingers pressed together, palms facing upward - creating a clean scoop to cradle the dipping ball.
rows.fault_trigger: BENDING AT THE WAIST - keeping the legs straight and simply leaning over. This ruins balance, alters eye level dramatically, and prevents running after the catch. THUMBS-UP MISTAKE - trying to catch a low ball with the thumbs together like a chest catch, forcing the hands upside down so the ball slips straight through onto the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the eyes hyper-focused on the hands and slide the inverted basket underneath the path of the ball, fingertips angled slightly upward right before impact, letting the ball land smoothly into the pinky basket while the fingers instantly curl around the leather.
rows.fault_trigger: EARLY EYES - snapping the head up to look at the defence while the ball is still inches from the pinkies, causing it to slip through the arms onto the grass. On a low catch there is no margin: the eyes must stay down until the fingers close.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward toward the stomach, cradling the ball securely against the body frame so it cannot slip out. The eyes stay locked on the ball as it transitions from the grass line up into the stomach - do not look up to run yet.
rows.fault_trigger: Looking up to run before the ball is rolled securely into the abdomen. The low catch is the least secure of all four, so any early upfield glance during the roll-up is how the ball ends up on the grass.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint at top speed along the route track with a steady, bounce-free head. Keep the hands down and relaxed while running, extending the arms upward only at the absolute last second to keep the trailing defender blind, then raise the hands near collarbone or chin level with pinkies pressed together and palms open to the sky, forming a deep running basket.
rows.fault_trigger: REACHING EARLY - running downfield with the arms extended to the sky for ten yards. This alerts the defender to play the arms, slows top sprint speed, and makes tracking the ball far harder. (Basket formation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The eyes track the nose of the ball dropping from the sky straight down into the open palms. The wrists stay completely loose and cushioned right before impact, letting the ball melt into the fingers without disrupting the running stride.
rows.fault_trigger: PEEKING - letting the head drift back forward toward the end zone just before the ball drops into the bucket, so it hits the helmet or falls straight through the hands. THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Clamp the fingers around the ball the instant it settles into the hands, pulling it straight down into the pocket arm position while the head stays rotated over the shoulder and the eyes stay locked on the hands until the ball is safely into the chest - all without breaking the vertical sprint into the end zone.
rows.fault_trigger: Snapping the head forward before the ball is secured into the chest pocket, so the catch is completed blind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans forward through the initial acceleration, driving the body out of the stance. The lean comes from the whole body angled forward, not from bending at the waist.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing straight up out of the stance, killing acceleration; or bending at the waist so the chest folds forward ahead of the hips instead of the whole body leaning.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise gradually across the first steps as speed builds, rather than popping upright immediately.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders spiking upright on the first step rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and slowing acceleration.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact is short and driving - the foot strikes underneath the body and leaves quickly, adding speed rather than absorbing it.
rows.fault_trigger: Long ground contact times, or the foot striking ahead of the body with backward velocity - braking on each step instead of driving.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
rows.fault_trigger: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the route develops.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet stay under the body through the first steps - narrow enough to run efficiently, wide enough to stay balanced through the acceleration.
rows.fault_trigger: Base widening through the first steps, costing efficiency and drive; or narrowing so far the receiver crosses over and loses balance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - with the elbows held at a consistent working angle to add drive out of the stance.
rows.fault_trigger: Arms out of sync with the legs, arms crossing the body's midline rather than driving forward and back, or elbows flailing/locking so the arms add no drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders stay connected to the hips and square to the release path, moving with the lower body rather than rotating independently of it.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating away from the hips and the release path, disconnecting upper and lower body and telegraphing the release direction.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay driving toward the release heading through the first steps, opening only as far as the release path requires.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips over-rotating off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground; or staying square when the release requires them to turn.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward through the first three steps, staying ahead of the base of support so each step drives rather than catches.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight stalling or moving backward relative to the feet, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head transitions from the inside snap cue to the release path and defensive target, turning under control without whipping or dropping.
rows.fault_trigger: Head whipping round or dropping during the release, or failing to transition from the ball to the release path. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the release begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
rows.fault_trigger: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the route begins.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the second step can build speed.
rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The body travels on a consistent, committed path off the line, matching the angle the called release requires - inside or outside - without drifting or rounding.
rows.fault_trigger: Drifting or rounding off the line rather than committing to a release angle. (Whether the angle matches the called release needs the route to be declared - not determinable from a solo clip.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the release - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
rows.fault_trigger: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward across the full 5 yards, staying ahead of the base of support so every step drives rather than catches.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight stalling or falling back behind the feet at any point in the 5 yards, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The base starts wider through the driving first steps, then narrows progressively into a linear running track by the fifth yard as the receiver transitions from acceleration to running.
rows.fault_trigger: Base staying wide through the whole 5 yards, costing efficiency and speed; or narrowing too early so the driving steps lose their power base.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays stable and level through the 5-yard drive, held steady enough to read the defender's leverage and cushion while the body accelerates.
rows.fault_trigger: Head bobbing, whipping or dropping through the drive, so the receiver cannot process the defender's leverage. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation and stability only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Each foot lands under or slightly behind the hips during the acceleration steps, so every strike drives the body forward instead of braking it.
rows.fault_trigger: Foot landing ahead of the hips at strike, creating a braking force that costs speed on every step - typically caused by overstriding out of the stance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver rolls off the front foot into the drive - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
rows.fault_trigger: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive front-to-back in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - at a consistent elbow angle, without swinging across the body.
rows.fault_trigger: Arms out of sync with the legs, swinging across the body's midline rather than driving front-to-back, or elbows flailing and locking so the arms add no drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Speed builds continuously across the first 5 yards - each step adds velocity, with no early plateau or stall in the acceleration.
rows.fault_trigger: Velocity plateauing early in the 5 yards, or stalling between steps - the receiver reaches a speed and stops building rather than accelerating through the stem. (Absolute rate needs a scale reference.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays quiet through the acceleration - shoulders and hips rotate only as much as the stride requires, so energy goes into forward drive rather than twisting.
rows.fault_trigger: Excessive torso rotation during max-effort strides - the shoulders counter-rotating hard against the hips, wasting energy that should go into forward drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the drive begins - the receiver goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
rows.fault_trigger: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the stem begins.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
rows.fault_trigger: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the route develops.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pads stay low out of the stance and rise smoothly and gradually across the 5 yards as speed builds, reaching upright running posture only once the acceleration phase is complete.
rows.fault_trigger: Popping upright prematurely rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and cutting acceleration short.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stride length expands progressively across the first 5 yards - short and driving at Step 1, opening up as speed builds through Steps 4 and 5.
rows.fault_trigger: Strides not expanding - staying short and choppy through the whole 5 yards; or opening up too early, overstriding out of the stance before speed supports it.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact shortens progressively across the 5 yards - longer on the driving first steps, then quicker as speed builds and the receiver transitions to running.
rows.fault_trigger: Ground contact times staying flat or lengthening across the 5 yards - the receiver is not converting drive into speed, and each step absorbs rather than adds velocity.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The stem holds a straight, committed line across the 5 yards - the body travels on the intended heading without drifting laterally, so the route develops on time and the break happens where it should.
rows.fault_trigger: Drifting laterally off the stem heading across the 5 yards, changing the depth and angle at which the break occurs. (Whether the heading matches the called route needs the route to be declared.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The torso holds an aggressive forward drive angle through the early steps - roughly 45 to 60 degrees from vertical - then transitions smoothly upfield as speed builds. The angle comes from the whole body driving forward, not from bending at the waist.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing too upright out of the stance, killing the drive angle; bending at the waist so the chest folds ahead of the hips; or holding the forward angle too long and failing to transition upfield.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the following steps can expand.
rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The base stays wide throughout the approach - noticeably wider than a running stride - so the receiver keeps blocking leverage and can react laterally to the defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Base narrowing into a normal running stride as the receiver closes, so he arrives with no lateral leverage and gets moved off the block on contact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver tracks a consistent line onto the defender, staying square to them so they cannot slip past inside or outside before the hands fit.
rows.fault_trigger: Drifting off the tracking line during the approach, so the defender slips past inside or outside before contact is made. (Alignment to the defender needs them in frame - path consistency only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The receiver closes the cushion under control - accelerating to eat up ground, then gathering before contact rather than running through the block at full speed.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-running the block - arriving at full speed with no gather, so the receiver loses balance on contact and the defender sheds him easily. (Cushion distance needs the defender in frame.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop into a loaded athletic squat before contact, establishing low leverage so the receiver arrives underneath the defender rather than upright.
rows.fault_trigger: Arriving tall and only sinking at or after contact, so the defender gets underneath the receiver's pads and uprights him immediately.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short, controlled and punchy, planting underneath the body's mass so power is available immediately rather than reaching out and losing the base.
rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass, which kills the power base and leaves the receiver reaching rather than driving.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips extend hard as the hands make contact, driving ground force up through the torso and into the defender so the block has power behind it rather than just reach.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands landing without hip extension behind them - an arms-only block with no ground force, which the defender sheds easily. Or the hips firing before the hands arrive, wasting the drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hands shoot forward violently at engagement, extending fast into the defender's chest frame rather than arriving late or short.
rows.fault_trigger: Slow or short hand extension, so the receiver makes contact with his chest rather than his hands and has no control of the defender. (Hand placement on the defender needs them in frame; grip needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: At engagement the shoulders stay low - at or below the defender's pad level - with the torso angled forward so the receiver wins the leverage battle rather than being stood up.
rows.fault_trigger: Engaging with pads high or the torso upright, letting the defender get underneath and upright the receiver, who then loses the block immediately. (Relative pad level needs the defender in frame.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The final two steps before contact shorten and quicken, keeping the feet under the body so the receiver can react instantly if the defender moves laterally.
rows.fault_trigger: Arriving on long strides rather than chopping the feet down, leaving the receiver committed and unable to adjust when the defender moves.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The knees hold a strong power angle - roughly 90 to 120 degrees - approaching and through impact, absorbing the collision and providing the platform to drive.
rows.fault_trigger: Knees straightening into contact, leaving the receiver stiff-legged with nothing to absorb the collision or drive through it; or collapsing so deep he cannot move his feet.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays up with the eyes on the target through contact - the receiver sees what he is blocking rather than ducking his head into the collision.
rows.fault_trigger: Dipping or ducking the head before contact - the receiver loses sight of the target and cannot adjust, and it is an unsafe way to take a collision. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The feet keep driving after contact, moving the defender while the base stays wide and the knees stay bent - the block is sustained rather than a single hit.
rows.fault_trigger: Stopping the feet on contact and leaning on the defender, or standing up and narrowing the base after the hit - either way the block is lost within a second.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The arms pump hard at chest height in a genuine sprint-start rhythm, matching what a real slant release would look like.
rows.fault_trigger: Passive or low-amplitude arm action that does not match a real sprint, leaving the upper body out of step with the feet and weakening the fake.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The drive leg holds an acute bend - roughly 110 to 130 degrees - producing maximum ground force to launch onto the diagonal.
rows.fault_trigger: Drive leg too straight at push-off, producing little ground force, so the attack step lacks the urgency needed to make the fake believable.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders rotate fully square to the 45 degree line with the torso driving low and forward, exactly as they would on a genuine slant.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders lagging behind the feet or staying upright rather than driving low onto the diagonal, so the upper body never commits to the lie.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips accelerate along the 45 degree path and rotate fully onto the inside diagonal, committing the whole body to the fake from the first step.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips staying square while only the feet take the diagonal, so the fake is not sold and a disciplined defender reads the outside release immediately.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The head locks straight down the 45 degree inside path from the first step, selling the route rather than checking on the defender.
rows.fault_trigger: LOOKING AT THE DEFENDER - peeking at the DB instead of locking down the 45 degree track, which breaks the illusion before it is established. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The back foot fires outward on a sharp 45 degree diagonal toward the inside lane, launching straight onto the diagonal track with no ground given up first.
rows.fault_trigger: SOFT FIRST STEP - taking a tentative, short step instead of an aggressive 45 degree launch. The receiver must look like he is sprinting a slant from step one. Also: losing ground backward before the step fires.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The torso stays low and forward in an aggressive sprinting posture through the push step, matching what a genuine slant would look like.
rows.fault_trigger: Torso rising toward upright during the push step, which tips that a plant is coming rather than a continued sprint inside.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips stay dropped and fully committed to the inside trajectory, holding the low sprinting position that makes the fake believable.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips rising through the push step, so the receiver looks like he is preparing to stop rather than sprinting a route - the defender reads the cut coming.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The back knee drives high and hard on the push step, simulating full sprint acceleration so nothing about the movement suggests a fake.
rows.fault_trigger: Low knee drive on the push step, betraying that the receiver is not truly accelerating and is already preparing to plant.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The head stays locked straight down the inside path through the push step, holding the deception right up until the plant.
rows.fault_trigger: Head turning back toward the outside before the plant, breaking the deception early and letting the defender sit on the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The arm pump continues at full amplitude through the push step, sustaining the impression of a slant or post being run at full effort.
rows.fault_trigger: Arm pump dropping off during the push step, which signals to the defender that the receiver is about to stop rather than continuing inside.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The opposite foot drives down the exact same 45 degree line as the first step, taking real ground inside so the fake reads as a committed route.
rows.fault_trigger: The second step drifting off the 45 degree line or shortening, so the diagonal track bends and the defender reads that the inside move is not real.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the third step the outside foot slams into the turf along the 45 degree line and grips, acting as a violent brake that kills the inside momentum in one contact.
rows.fault_trigger: The plant foot sliding or drifting at contact rather than gripping, so the momentum is not arrested and the receiver needs extra steps to change direction.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The head holds the inside fake alignment right up to the exact plant frame, then prepares to snap back - the deception is maintained to the last possible instant.
rows.fault_trigger: Head starting to turn back outside before the plant lands, giving the defender an early warning and letting them jump the breakout. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The outside hand crosses over the chest frame at the plant, shielding the body against any late contact from a defender closing on the fake.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands staying wide or low at the plant, leaving the chest unprotected at the exact moment a defender who bought the fake is arriving. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The planting knee flexes deep - roughly 90 to 110 degrees - creating a spring-loaded platform to drive back out toward the sideline.
rows.fault_trigger: Planting on a stiff, straight leg, which cannot absorb the momentum or store energy - the receiver slides through the cut and the breakout has no power.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips drop sharply and shift slightly back at the plant, sinking to absorb the forward momentum and load the push back outside.
rows.fault_trigger: POP-UP BRAKING - letting the chest and hips rise when trying to stop. Without sinking the hips to absorb the momentum, the receiver slides or stumbles instead of cutting cleanly.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The shoulders stay over the toes as the plant foot lands, keeping the body stacked over the brake and ready to snap back toward the outside.
rows.fault_trigger: Chest rising or the shoulders falling behind the plant foot, so the weight sits back and the receiver cannot push cleanly back to the outside.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The trailing arm executes a heavy downward chop past the shoulder line, clearing the defender's arms as the receiver breaks back to the outside.
rows.fault_trigger: No hand action at the breakout, or an arm path that never crosses the shoulder line, leaving a recovering defender's hands attached through the escape. (Specific hand technique needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The outside knee drives high toward the sideline and upfield, taking immediate ground and building instant separation out of the cut.
rows.fault_trigger: Low knee drive out of the breakout, so the first strides are short and the receiver takes too long to convert the cut into separation.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The inside shoulder rolls away from the defender as the receiver breaks out, turning the chest off them and eliminating the jersey surface they could grab.
rows.fault_trigger: LEAVING THE CHEST EXPOSED - turning back outside with the chest wide open, which invites a trailing defender to land a heavy recovery punch and push the receiver off his path.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The plant foot drives explosively back toward the outside, the step reversing direction sharply enough to complete the diamond path and escape into the open lane.
rows.fault_trigger: A rounded or gradual change of direction rather than a sharp reversal, so the diamond flattens into a curve and the defender recovers the ground the fake bought.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The hips snap violently open toward the sideline, flipping the body off the inside track and onto the outside release in one decisive rotation.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips opening slowly or only partway, so the receiver drifts out of the cut rather than exploding, and the separation the fake created is given straight back.
