rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive off the line at full velocity for 10-12 yards with pads leaning forward and natural full strides, forcing the defender into an aggressive backpedal for fear of the go route. Two steps before break depth, violently sink the hips and chop the cleats to control speed - without standing up or slowing the arm pump.
rows.fault_trigger: THE DEAD GIVEAWAY - slowing the arm pump or raising the chest before reaching break depth, alerting the defender to clamp down on the out route. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the declared route.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of deceleration, snap the head and eyes sharply toward the sideline first. The visual turn shifts equilibrium and opens the upper torso toward the boundary before the feet leave the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: Head turning at the same time as the plant or after it, so the body commits before the eyes have opened the boundary - the torso does not pre-rotate and the break is slower. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: As the eyes find the boundary, slam the inside foot down into a tight, compact step directly under the centre of mass. The toe is pulled up sharply into dorsiflexion right before contact, striking with a rigid foot to lock the brakes. Instantly pivot and point the toe down a flat 90-degree track toward the sideline, masking the break until the last possible instant.
rows.fault_trigger: THE LUNGING SLIDE - lunging too far forward with a loose, downward-pointing toe. The over-extension lacks the rigidity to anchor a 90-degree turn, so the shoe slides over the grass and the defender closes the gap.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Push violently off the inside instep of the directing foot, flip the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate flat along the 90-degree line toward the sideline.
rows.fault_trigger: DRIFTING DOWNHILL - allowing the route to angle backward toward the line of scrimmage. The line must stay flat and parallel to the line of scrimmage to keep outrunning the trailing defender.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint hard downfield for 10-12 yards (12-15 on the deeper variation), pushing the vertical stem straight through the defender's outside shoulder to force them to protect the deep outside lane. One step before the break, drop the weight subtly into the hips and prepare to transfer laterally - without any choppy or gathering steps.
rows.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before making the actual break. A rounded line lets an inside-shade defender stay in front of the receiver the whole way. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference and the called depth.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: At the peak of the stem, snap the head and eyes around to face the near goal post first. The visual snap opens the torso and clears vision to read the safety rotation before the body commits.
rows.fault_trigger: Head turning with the plant or after it rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks inside without having read the safety rotation and the torso never pre-rotates. (Gaze and safety position are not pose-measurable.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The millisecond the eyes locate the post, drive the OUTSIDE cutting foot down into a compact step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled upward into dorsiflexion right before contact to establish a firm ankle lock. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly pointing the toe at a sharp 45-degree angle toward the post.
rows.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive powerfully off the inside instep of the directing foot, snap the hips wide open, and punch the outside arm across the body to accelerate down the 45-degree track, holding a low, aggressive acceleration posture.
rows.fault_trigger: FLATTENING THE ROUTE - letting the route drift flat toward the opposite sideline instead of holding a true 45-degree angle toward the goal post, which takes the receiver out of the intended throwing window.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode off the ball with a violent, low pad-level release to clear the press defender's hands and establish a strict linear track down the hashes or the seam lane, then transition smoothly into top-end sprint posture with stride lengths opening to maximum expansion, chin tucked and core locked on the track.
rows.fault_trigger: BAILING OFF-TRACK - drifting wide toward the sideline or inside toward the middle right off the snap. Scurrying off the track ruins the spacing of the concept and runs the receiver straight into zone defenders.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pushing through the intermediate zone at 10-12 yards, expect a collision or squeeze from interior linebackers or safeties. Use a high-speed hand swipe, chop or arm bar to clear their contact while holding the vertical line without drifting off-track or losing a step.
rows.fault_trigger: SLOWING DOWN FOR CONTACT - decelerating or stutter-stepping when an inside linebacker tries to reroute or jam. The receiver must sprint through the contact and use the hands to clear without dropping speed. (Defender contact is not pose-measurable.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Squeeze tightly into the defensive void with the running track completely straight. Steps stay compact and directly beneath the centre of mass without overstriding, toes pulling up into sharp dorsiflexion on every stride for a rigid ankle lock, while the eyes track the ball over the inside shoulder.
rows.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING / FLOPPY FOOTWORK - reaching too far forward to try to outrun a deep safety, or running with a loose, downward-pointing toe. This strips core stability and caps top-end speed. Also: drifting laterally out of the void.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Expect a heavy hit from a closing safety or linebacker over the middle. Keep the hands down late to mask the ball's arrival, then shoot the arms up violently to snap the ball out of the air at its highest point, instantly tucking it to protect against incoming contact.
rows.fault_trigger: EXPOSING THE BALL - catching with the body loose or waiting for the ball to hit the chest. Over the middle, failing to snatch with extended hands and instantly tuck results in drops and forced fumbles. (Ball position and contact are not pose-measurable.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fire off the line hard for 3 direct vertical strides in a fierce sprint-sell posture - the path must look identical to a go route to freeze the defender's feet and leverage. On the second step, subtly drop the hips an inch into a compact athletic posture while the feet keep moving at full velocity.
rows.fault_trigger: BANANA STEMMING - curving the path inward before the actual break, letting an inside-shade defender stay in front the whole way. CHOPPING FEET - gathering or stutter-stepping before the break; a slant relies entirely on pure unmitigated speed, and chopping ruins the separation.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: At the exact peak of the third stride, snap the head and eyes inside across the middle of the field first. The visual snap instantly clears vision to read the inside linebackers and pick up the ball's release.
rows.fault_trigger: Head turning with or after the plant rather than leading it, so the receiver breaks across the defender's face without having cleared his vision - and on a route this quick, the ball is often already out. (Gaze and defender positions are not pose-measurable.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The split-second the eyes turn, drive the outside foot down into a controlled step tightly aligned within the frame. The toe is pulled up into dorsiflexion before impact to establish a firm ankle lock, and the step is not overextended. The cleat slams down directly beneath the hips, instantly directing the toe at a sharp 45 degrees toward the middle to slice across the defender's face without losing linear body control.
rows.fault_trigger: OVERSTRIDING THE BREAK - reaching too far inside with a long, diving step. This elongates the body frame, tells the defender exactly when the break is coming, and locks up the hips so the receiver cannot accelerate smoothly out of the cut.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the body weight smoothly off the directing foot, punch the outside arm violently across the body to hold top sprinting speed, maintain the 45-degree trajectory, and catch the ball cleanly in stride.
rows.fault_trigger: RUNNING FLAT - flattening the route out horizontally toward the opposite sideline. The receiver must hold a strict 45-degree angle to keep outrunning the trailing defender. (Ball location needs ball tracking.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain controlled and aligned with the intended release position. The upper body should not rotate excessively away from the line before movement begins.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotated away from the line before the snap, telegraphing the release direction to the defender, or shoulder line unlevel enough to unbalance the first step.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Front knee is bent rather than locked. The knee tracks forward toward the toe while maintaining an athletic loaded position. Rear knee remains flexed enough to contribute to the first movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Front knee locked or straight, knee collapsing inside or outside the toe line, or rear knee too extended to contribute to the first movement.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head is turned inside toward the football before the snap, with eyes locked onto the ball. The receiver uses the football's movement as the visual snap cue rather than reacting to the quarterback's verbal cadence. Head position remains controlled and stable so the receiver can explode immediately when the ball is snapped without a false start.
rows.fault_trigger: Head facing straight downfield rather than turned inside to the ball, or head unstable/bobbing pre-snap so the receiver reacts late. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only. Ball location needs ball tracking.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Inside foot is forward, toward the ball. Feet maintain the appropriate stagger and orientation to allow the receiver to release without a false step. The front foot carries a very slight inward turn - enough to aid the release, but not so much that the turn carries up into the hips and opens them inside. The front foot supports the initial roll-off movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Outside foot forward instead of the inside foot; stagger too deep or too shallow to release cleanly; front toe square or turned outward rather than slightly in; or the inward turn overdone so it pulls the hips inside and opens them before the snap. (Which foot is 'inside' depends on alignment side - not determinable from a solo clip.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receiver remains stable but immediately movable. The stance is sufficiently loaded to prevent a false step while allowing explosive movement in the intended release direction.
rows.fault_trigger: Swaying, rocking, or bouncing pre-snap rather than settling into a loaded position; or so rigid and locked that the first movement requires a reset. A false step at the snap is the downstream symptom.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet are approximately shoulder width apart, providing a stable and explosive base. The stance is wide enough for balance without restricting the first step.
rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow to balance, or so wide it restricts the first step and forces a false step to recover.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hands remain relaxed, uncrossed, and independent. Hands are positioned near the waist or slightly higher in front of the chest depending on anticipated coverage. Hands remain free to immediately react to a press defender.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands crossed over the body's midline, clamped tight to the torso, or held so low or high that the receiver cannot react to a press. Arms rigid rather than relaxed. (Finger and grip detail needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Approximately 70-80% of body weight is loaded onto the front leg. The rear leg remains available to contribute to the release. The receiver should be able to roll forward off the front foot without rocking backward or taking a false step.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight sitting back on the rear leg or evenly split, forcing a backward rock or false step before the release.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Chest and hips are lowered into an athletic position. The shoulders/chest are positioned over the front knee, creating forward readiness without excessive crouching.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing too tall with no forward readiness, or crouching so low the receiver cannot release cleanly. Chest behind or well past the front knee.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded underneath the torso and prepared to drive toward the release. Hips should not be excessively opened before movement begins.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips opened toward the release before movement begins, giving away direction, or hips drifting out from under the torso so the drive is weakened.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Upper body is positioned at approximately the same forward angle as the loaded front shin, creating a connected lower- and upper-body position. Avoid excessive bending at the waist.
rows.fault_trigger: Torso angle diverging from the shin angle - typically folding forward at the waist with the chest well ahead of the shin line, or standing the torso upright while the shin stays loaded, disconnecting upper and lower body.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align as an attached, "in-line" tight end, establishing a balanced foundation to support both heavy run blocking and explosive short pass routes.
Place the down hand firmly on the turf (typically the hand closest to the ball), loading enough weight to trigger forward burst without becoming top-heavy.
Stagger the back foot slightly (toe-to-instep or toe-to-heel), keeping the heel elevated to load the calf and Achilles like a coiled spring.
rows.fault_trigger: Flat Backside Foot. Letting the heel of the staggered back foot drop completely flat to the turf, which delays the initial forward step and ruins explosive drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips to establish a low, explosive center of gravity optimized for immediate leverage against heavier defensive ends.
rows.fault_trigger: "Tail-Skying" / Too Much Forward Weight. Setting the hips too high or loading too much weight onto the down hand, which causes the tight end to stumble forward or immediately drop their head upon snapping out of the stance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the head up and neck relaxed, looking through the eyebrows to scan the immediate edge defender and linebackers.
Align as a flexed "F" tight end, split out in the slot, or slightly off the line of scrimmage in a balanced, upright posture.
Stand with a slight stagger, feet shoulder-width apart, keeping the weight evenly distributed on the balls of the feet.
Hinge at the hips and slightly bend the knees to create a coiled, athletic quarter-squat, rather than standing rigidly straight.
rows.fault_trigger: "Standing Tall". Keeping the knees straight and waist unhinged, which raises the pad level and makes the tight end an easy target for defenders to jam or blow off the line of scrimmage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Chamber the hands actively near the waist or chest, keeping them completely unweighted and ready to punch or hand-fight on a release.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands on Thighs. Resting the hands heavily on the thighs pre-snap, which slows down the punch reaction time on a block or delayed release.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Utilize the upright vision to clearly read the defensive front, second-level linebackers, and safety rotations before the snap.
Lock into an in-line 3-point stance, directly identifying the edge rusher or blitzing outside linebacker threatening the perimeter.
Pop up rapidly out of the dirt on the snap, replacing the down hand with an instant lateral or backward step to set the edge.
rows.fault_trigger: "Lunging from the Dirt". Diving forward at the defender's waist out of the stance, which allows an athletic edge rusher to effortlessly slip the block with a quick swim or club-and-rip move.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a wide, stable low-man leverage base, centering the incoming heavy edge rusher squarely between the knees.
rows.fault_trigger: Heel Clicking. Bringing the feet together while trying to kick or slide laterally, destroying balance and leaving the tight end helpless against a heavy bull rush.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fire violent, tight hands inside the defender's chest plate/framework while keeping the elbows tucked to absorb kinetic power.
Sink the hips deeply, anchoring against the heavy bull rush while keeping the feet active to secure the perimeter of the pocket.
Align in a flexed 2-point stance, visually tracking the designated speed rusher, blitzer, or wide-9 defensive end.
Push off the inside foot instantly, using the upright advantage to execute an immediate lateral slide to widen the pocket.
rows.fault_trigger: Passive "Catching". Standing frozen in place and letting the defender dictate the physical contact, which compresses the edge of the pocket directly into the quarterback.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the shoulders square and sink the hips, aggressively mirroring the rusher to force them wide and around the pocket's deep arc.
rows.fault_trigger: Bailing the Hips. Turning the toes and opening the hips outward too early, which instantly concedes a soft inside path straight into the B-gap.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Utilize active, independent hands to punch the defender's near cylinder, instantly disrupting their speed and trajectory.
Keep the feet sliding continuously, ensuring the defender cannot turn the corner or execute a sudden inside counter-move to the B-gap.
Set an aggressive in-line 3-point stance, targeting the down-lineman or edge setter for a heavy base, reach, or down block.
Explode forward and upward directly from the dirt, taking a powerful, ground-gaining first step to close the cushion instantly.
Track the first power step directly through the center mass of the defender, dropping the hips below the defender's pad level.
Shoot the hands violently straight up into the armpits and inside frame of the defender, locking out the elbows.
rows.fault_trigger: Head Dropping. Dropping the chin to the chest upon contact, which breaks the spine angle, eliminates vision, and causes the tight end to slide right off the defender.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive the legs relentlessly, churning the feet to physically displace the edge of the defense and clear the primary running lane.
rows.fault_trigger: Pop and Stop. Landing a powerful initial punch but immediately stopping all foot movement, which allows the defender to shed the block and make the tackle.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align in a 2-point stance, optimizing vision to execute space or perimeter blocks (reach block on wide zone, or kick-out on a slice/split-zone).
Take fast, ground-gaining lateral steps off the snap, leveraging the upright stance to instantly close horizontal distance.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-stepping Flat. Taking an initial step that is too wide and flat on a zone play, allowing a quick interior defender to shoot underneath and disrupt the backfield.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink the hips and bend the knees during the approach to establish a low, powerful striking angle before contact is made.
rows.fault_trigger: Waist Bending. Reaching forward for a defender by bending at the waist instead of sinking the hips and bending the knees, resulting in a weak, off-balance block.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a violent, fundamentally sound block, either sealing the outside shoulder on a reach, or delivering a heavy inside-shoulder strike on a kick-out.
Unceasingly run the feet upon contact, steering the defender entirely out of the run track or completely sealing the edge.
Align tightly attached or in a wing position, noting both the immediate edge rusher (the chip target) and the intended pass route.
Explode off the line simulating a true run block, closing the gap directly into the edge rusher to force them to brace for heavy contact.
Deliver a physical, stalling blow directly into the rusher's ribs, shoulder, or chest to violently disrupt their momentum and assist the offensive tackle.
rows.fault_trigger: The "Whiff" / Soft Contact. Running past the defender or delivering a weak arm-swipe that fails to disrupt the rusher's track, leaving the offensive tackle out of position.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The exact moment the heavy contact lands, seamlessly detach and slip past the defender's outside or inside hip without getting grabbed.
rows.fault_trigger: "Sticky Contact". Getting physically entangled or staying locked onto the defender for too long, which ruins the timing of the pass play and prevents the tight end from getting open.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Accelerate instantly from the chip, re-establishing vertical route speed and getting eyes quickly to the quarterback.
Pads stay low out of the stance and rise gradually across the first steps as speed builds, rather than popping upright immediately.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders spiking upright on the first step rather than rising gradually, losing the forward drive angle and slowing acceleration.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The torso leans forward through the initial acceleration, driving the body out of the stance. The lean comes from the whole body angled forward, not from bending at the waist.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing straight up out of the stance, killing acceleration; or bending at the waist so the chest folds forward ahead of the hips instead of the whole body leaning.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ground contact is short and driving - the foot strikes underneath the body and leaves quickly, adding speed rather than absorbing it.
rows.fault_trigger: Long ground contact times, or the foot striking ahead of the body with backward velocity - braking on each step instead of driving.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step travels directly along the intended release heading, without lateral drift that costs ground or telegraphs the release direction.
rows.fault_trigger: First step drifting laterally off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground before the route develops.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet stay under the body through the first steps - narrow enough to run efficiently, wide enough to stay balanced through the acceleration.
rows.fault_trigger: Base widening through the first steps, costing efficiency and drive; or narrowing so far the tight end crosses over and loses balance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Arms drive in rhythm with the legs - opposite arm to opposite leg - with the elbows held at a consistent working angle to add drive out of the stance.
rows.fault_trigger: Arms out of sync with the legs, arms crossing the body's midline rather than driving forward and back, or elbows flailing/locking so the arms add no drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders stay connected to the hips and square to the release path, moving with the lower body rather than rotating independently of it.
rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders rotating away from the hips and the release path, disconnecting upper and lower body and telegraphing the release direction.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips stay driving toward the release heading through the first steps, opening only as far as the release path requires.
rows.fault_trigger: Hips over-rotating off the release heading, widening the path and costing ground; or staying square when the release requires them to turn.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight moves continuously forward through the first three steps, staying ahead of the base of support so each step drives rather than catches.
rows.fault_trigger: Weight stalling or moving backward relative to the feet, so a step catches the body instead of driving it forward.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head transitions from the inside snap cue to the release path and defensive target, turning under control without whipping or dropping.
rows.fault_trigger: Head whipping round or dropping during the release, or failing to transition from the ball to the release path. (Gaze itself is not pose-measurable - orientation only.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first movement travels forward along the release heading. No backward or lateral step is taken before the release begins - the tight end goes directly from the loaded stance into the first step.
rows.fault_trigger: A false step - a backward or sideways step before the first forward step - losing ground and time before the route begins.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The first step is short and driving rather than long and reaching - it establishes ground contact quickly and underneath the body so the second step can build speed.
rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding on the first step so the foot lands ahead of the body's mass and brakes rather than drives; or a step so short it fails to create separation.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The body travels on a consistent, committed path off the line, matching the angle the called release requires - inside or outside - without drifting or rounding.
rows.fault_trigger: Drifting or rounding off the line rather than committing to a release angle. (Whether the angle matches the called release needs the route to be declared - not determinable from a solo clip.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The tight end rolls off the front foot into the release - the heel lifts while the toe stays in contact, driving the body forward. The roll-off leads the forward travel rather than following it.
rows.fault_trigger: Backward weight transfer before the roll-off, the whole foot leaving the ground flat rather than rolling through the toe, or excessive vertical rise instead of forward drive.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish an upright stance, ensuring no preliminary tells are given to the defense regarding whether a block or route is imminent.
Lock into the attached, in-line 3-point position, loading the lower body for a low-to-high transition.
Push violently off the inside ball of the back foot to initiate explosive forward acceleration.
rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping". Picking up the lead foot and dropping it in place, or taking a slight step backward with the back foot before moving forward, which delays the start of the play.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Drive the lead foot forward to gain a concise, efficient 6-to-12 inches of ground.
Keep the chin tucked and the chest forward, ensuring the spine angle strictly matches the pre-snap posture without rising.
rows.fault_trigger: Standing Straight Up. Raising the head and shoulders on the very first step, which exposes the chest to a defender's jam and eliminates all low-man leverage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Rip the hands out from their relaxed pre-snap position, driving the elbows back aggressively to synchronize with the lower body.
Explode out of the stance by uncoiling the hips and driving the back foot forcefully into the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: Tail-Skying. Lifting the hips straight up into the air on the first step instead of driving the hips forward through the block or release.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Whip the down hand completely off the ground the exact millisecond the foot movement begins.
rows.fault_trigger: "Sticking the Hand". Failing to pick up the down hand smoothly, which causes the tight end to lunge forward, lose their footing, and fall to their knees.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Launch both hands forward immediately into a chambered, ready position to deliver a heavy strike or swat a defender's jam.
Execute a short, punchy power step while tracking the feet wide on parallel tracks to establish total stability upon contact.
Instantly secure the catch in space and transition the ball directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field turn before the ball is possessed.
rows.fault_trigger: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or turn up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.
rows.fault_trigger: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.
rows.fault_trigger: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Read interior pursuit and transfer the ball to the outside arm (closest to the sideline), freeing the inside arm to stiff-arm or guard against incoming tacklers.
The moment traffic closes in or a tackle is initiated, wrap the off-hand over the ball (two-handed carry) and chin the football to protect it completely through the ground.

Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.
rows.fault_trigger: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Intercept the nose of the ball out wide in the centre of the diamond, elbows unlocked to absorb the high-velocity lateral momentum. The nose must be pointed exactly at the hands at the moment of impact - not tracking the ball peripherally.
rows.fault_trigger: THE PERIPHERAL PEEK - trying to catch using only peripheral vision with the nose pointed straight downfield, which ruins hand-eye coordination and depth perception. THE STIFF LATERAL LOCKOUT - catching out wide with locked elbows, so the ball clanks off rigid fingertips.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sweep the ball back tightly across the body into the core ribcage, instantly snapping the chin down and across the torso to visually lock the ball into the tuck position before looking upfield.
rows.fault_trigger: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.
rows.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently across the chest, rolling the head diagonally downward to visually track the ball all the way from the high-outside quadrant into chest protection as the feet return to the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.
rows.fault_trigger: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inverted hands underneath the dipping path of the ball, with the chin tucked to the catch-side shoulder and the eyes glued to the grass-level pinky basket as the ball settles in.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes lifting off the basket before the fingers close. On a low-and-wide catch the hands are at their furthest from the head, so peripheral tracking is at its least reliable and the margin is smallest.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.
rows.fault_trigger: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold a strong base with the eyes locked on the point of the ball. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.
rows.fault_trigger: BODY CATCHING - letting the ball travel all the way into the chest pads instead of extending the hands, so it bounces off hard plastic armour and results in drops or deflections. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Let the nose of the ball enter the centre of the diamond while the eyes stay hyper-focused on the leather. The elbows stay relaxed and flexible to give with the ball and absorb its force, with the fingertips - not the palms - clamping the panels.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY LOOK - snapping the head up to look at an oncoming defender right before the ball hits the hands, causing a ricochet off the fingertips. THE STIFF-ARM CLANK - catching with locked-out elbows and hard palms; without joint elasticity a fast ball clanks off the hands. (Ball contact needs object detection.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball tightly back into the ribcage, wrapping the arm completely over it for a four-point pressure hold. Instantly drop the chin to visually confirm the catch - nose to the tuck - before snapping the eyes upfield to look for defenders.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes leaving the ball before the tuck is complete - the head comes up to find defenders while the ball is still being secured, which is how a clean catch becomes a fumble. Also: no chin drop at all, so the catch is never visually confirmed.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high trajectory and time the jump or extension so the hands intercept the ball at the absolute apex of reach. Shoot both arms violently upward above the forehead with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs pressed tightly together and index fingers pointing up, creating an inverted triangle to look through.
rows.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES OUT - reaching up for a high ball with the pinkies together instead of the thumbs. This turns the palms away from the ball and makes a clean high catch impossible. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stare directly through the window created by the hands and pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible point, fingers spread wide and thumbs facing each other right before impact, fingertips wrapping tightly around the tip and sides to halt its momentum mid-air.
rows.fault_trigger: THE BLIND PULL - tilting the head back down toward the turf before the hands secure the ball, resulting in a blind, clapping attempt at the apex. CLAPPING AT THE BALL - slapping the hands together from the sides; if the timing is off by a millisecond the palms hit the ball and knock it away.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently to the chest as the feet return to the turf, the head snapping down to follow the ball's descent from the sky straight into the core, then immediately roll the body or shoulders over the ball to protect it from closing defenders.
rows.fault_trigger: Head staying tilted up after the catch rather than following the ball down into the body, so the tuck is never visually confirmed. Also: landing stiff-legged without knee flexion, costing balance and the ability to run after the catch.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the downward trajectory and lower the entire body frame by bending at the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist. Drop the arms toward the grass with elbows tucked close to the torso, then invert the hands completely - pinky fingers pressed together, palms facing upward - creating a clean scoop to cradle the dipping ball.
rows.fault_trigger: BENDING AT THE WAIST - keeping the legs straight and simply leaning over. This ruins balance, alters eye level dramatically, and prevents running after the catch. THUMBS-UP MISTAKE - trying to catch a low ball with the thumbs together like a chest catch, forcing the hands upside down so the ball slips straight through onto the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the eyes hyper-focused on the hands and slide the inverted basket underneath the path of the ball, fingertips angled slightly upward right before impact, letting the ball land smoothly into the pinky basket while the fingers instantly curl around the leather.
rows.fault_trigger: EARLY EYES - snapping the head up to look at the defence while the ball is still inches from the pinkies, causing it to slip through the arms onto the grass. On a low catch there is no margin: the eyes must stay down until the fingers close.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward toward the stomach, cradling the ball securely against the body frame so it cannot slip out. The eyes stay locked on the ball as it transitions from the grass line up into the stomach - do not look up to run yet.
rows.fault_trigger: Looking up to run before the ball is rolled securely into the abdomen. The low catch is the least secure of all four, so any early upfield glance during the roll-up is how the ball ends up on the grass.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint at top speed along the route track with a steady, bounce-free head. Keep the hands down and relaxed while running, extending the arms upward only at the absolute last second to keep the trailing defender blind, then raise the hands near collarbone or chin level with pinkies pressed together and palms open to the sky, forming a deep running basket.
rows.fault_trigger: REACHING EARLY - running downfield with the arms extended to the sky for ten yards. This alerts the defender to play the arms, slows top sprint speed, and makes tracking the ball far harder. (Basket formation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The eyes track the nose of the ball dropping from the sky straight down into the open palms. The wrists stay completely loose and cushioned right before impact, letting the ball melt into the fingers without disrupting the running stride.
rows.fault_trigger: PEEKING - letting the head drift back forward toward the end zone just before the ball drops into the bucket, so it hits the helmet or falls straight through the hands. THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Clamp the fingers around the ball the instant it settles into the hands, pulling it straight down into the pocket arm position while the head stays rotated over the shoulder and the eyes stay locked on the hands until the ball is safely into the chest - all without breaking the vertical sprint into the end zone.
rows.fault_trigger: Snapping the head forward before the ball is secured into the chest pocket, so the catch is completed blind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the catch in space and transition the ball directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field turn before the ball is possessed.
rows.fault_trigger: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or turn up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.
rows.fault_trigger: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.
rows.fault_trigger: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Read interior pursuit and transfer the ball to the outside arm (closest to the sideline), freeing the inside arm to stiff-arm or guard against incoming tacklers.
The moment traffic closes in or a tackle is initiated, wrap the off-hand over the ball (two-handed carry) and chin the football to protect it completely through the ground.

Hold the running trajectory and snap the eyes toward the incoming ball, judging its lateral path while keeping stride length intact. Fire BOTH arms outward away from the torso into the lateral lane, torquing the upper chest slightly toward the ball without breaking the lower body's running line, and form a tight diamond out wide with thumbs and index fingers connected and palms squared to the side-angle trajectory.
rows.fault_trigger: REACHING WITH ONE HAND - extending only the leading arm, cutting the catching surface in half. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Intercept the nose of the ball out wide in the centre of the diamond, elbows unlocked to absorb the high-velocity lateral momentum. The nose must be pointed exactly at the hands at the moment of impact - not tracking the ball peripherally.
rows.fault_trigger: THE PERIPHERAL PEEK - trying to catch using only peripheral vision with the nose pointed straight downfield, which ruins hand-eye coordination and depth perception. THE STIFF LATERAL LOCKOUT - catching out wide with locked elbows, so the ball clanks off rigid fingertips.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sweep the ball back tightly across the body into the core ribcage, instantly snapping the chin down and across the torso to visually lock the ball into the tuck position before looking upfield.
rows.fault_trigger: The head snapping back downfield while the ball is still being swept across the body, so the rotational momentum of the sweep pulls the eyes off the leather and the ball is lost mid-transfer.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the high, fading trajectory and time the jump or upper-body extension to meet the ball out wide at its highest point. Shoot both arms violently upward and outward on a 45-degree diagonal with elbows slightly flexed, hands open wide with thumbs locked together and index fingers pointing diagonally upward to form the overhead triangle.
rows.fault_trigger: TURNING PINKIES UP - reaching up and out with the pinkies together, which turns the palms completely away from the ball's path. THE OVERHEAD CLAP - slapping the hands together laterally from the sides instead of clamping the ball's incoming line. (Hand orientation needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pluck the ball out of the air at its highest possible lateral apex, staring directly through the diagonal window formed by the hands. The head must not drift back toward the centre of the body before the ball is secured.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY CENTRE DROP - catching the ball diagonally but snapping the head back to the centre of the field before pulling it down, leading to a blind tuck and a high chance of dropping it on turf impact.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pull the ball down violently across the chest, rolling the head diagonally downward to visually track the ball all the way from the high-outside quadrant into chest protection as the feet return to the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: The head returning to centre or upfield before the ball reaches the chest, completing the tuck blind - the most common way a spectacular high-and-wide catch becomes a drop on landing.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Track the low, diving path and drop the entire body level by bending deeply at the knees and hips. Drop both arms diagonally downward toward the grass on the catch side with elbows tucked near the lower ribcage, inverting the hands out to the side - pinky fingers pressed tightly together, palms facing upward and outward - to form a secure under-scoop.
rows.fault_trigger: WAIST-BENDING REACHES - keeping the legs straight and bending sideways at the waist, which destroys balance and pulls the eyes away from the ball. THUMBS-TOGETHER LOW CATCH - trying to scoop a low-lateral ball with the thumbs together, forcing the palms to face the ground. (Hand inversion needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slide the inverted hands underneath the dipping path of the ball, with the chin tucked to the catch-side shoulder and the eyes glued to the grass-level pinky basket as the ball settles in.
rows.fault_trigger: Eyes lifting off the basket before the fingers close. On a low-and-wide catch the hands are at their furthest from the head, so peripheral tracking is at its least reliable and the margin is smallest.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Roll the hands and forearms upward and across the stomach, keeping the head down and rotated laterally. Watch the ball leave the lateral plane and physically touch the stomach before the eyes snap up to run.
rows.fault_trigger: THE UP-AND-OUT PULL - catching the ball low and wide but immediately pulling the head up and away to look at a defender, so the ball slips out of the pinkies during the lateral sweep. The longest, least secure transfer of any catch in the set.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold a strong base with the eyes locked on the point of the ball. Shoot the arms forward away from the jersey to meet the ball early and maximise the catching radius, forming a tight symmetric diamond with thumbs and index fingers pressed together and palms turned outward to face the incoming ball.
rows.fault_trigger: BODY CATCHING - letting the ball travel all the way into the chest pads instead of extending the hands, so it bounces off hard plastic armour and results in drops or deflections. (Hand shape needs the Hand landmarker.)

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Let the nose of the ball enter the centre of the diamond while the eyes stay hyper-focused on the leather. The elbows stay relaxed and flexible to give with the ball and absorb its force, with the fingertips - not the palms - clamping the panels.
rows.fault_trigger: THE EARLY LOOK - snapping the head up to look at an oncoming defender right before the ball hits the hands, causing a ricochet off the fingertips. THE STIFF-ARM CLANK - catching with locked-out elbows and hard palms; without joint elasticity a fast ball clanks off the hands. (Ball contact needs object detection.)

THE PALMS-FORWARD BARRIER - facing the palms toward the line of scrimmage instead of up to the sky, creating a wall the ball bounces off rather than a basket it falls into.

rows.fault_trigger: Snapping the head forward before the ball is secured into the chest pocket, so the catch is completed blind.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced, comfortable 2-point stance to ensure a clear, unobstructed view of the defensive front and linebackers.
Establish a wide, stable foundation by setting the feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with a distinct toe-to-heel stagger.
Push violently off the back foot from a deep alignment (5 to 7 yards behind the QB), driving the lead foot forward 6 to 12 inches.
rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping". Dropping the back foot further backward or picking up the lead foot and placing it down in the exact same spot before moving forward, ruining the timing of the mesh.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Firing from an alignment parallel to the quarterback, pivot strictly on the inside foot (closest to the QB).
Operating from roughly 3 yards directly behind the shotgun QB, take a hard, single direct step forward with the lead foot.
rows.fault_trigger: "Dancing". Hesitating or taking multiple short, choppy steps at the snap instead of committing to a single, violent first step.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode forward out of the 3-point stance by physically rolling the body weight over the front knee.
rows.fault_trigger: "False Stepping". Pivoting or dropping the rear foot further backward before launching forward, which delays the block and completely destroys the timing of the running back's path.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set feet strictly shoulder-width apart, keeping toes straight ahead with an optional, slight toe-to-instep stagger based on personal comfort.
rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing". Shifting weight onto the toes when running a play to that side, or leaning back slightly on passing downs, giving away the play pre-snap.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sink into a relaxed quarter-squat, keeping the lower body completely loose and uncoiled for multi-directional responsiveness.
Keep the chest up, the back completely flat, and the chin tucked to see the line of scrimmage through the top of the visor.
Rest hands loosely on the upper thighs with elbows bent and tucked close to the ribs, ready to instantly form a ball pocket or strike a blitzer.
rows.fault_trigger: Hands on Knees. Locking the elbows out and resting the upper-body weight heavily on the knees, which delays hand usage for pass protection or taking a clean handoff exchange.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the hand corresponding to the back foot down on the turf, positioned slightly inside the framework of the knee.
Rest minimal weight (roughly 20%) onto the fingertips of the down hand to avoid lunging on the snap.
rows.fault_trigger: Heavy Hand Loading. Putting too much body weight onto the fingers of the down hand, causing the blocker to trip forward or lunge on their first step.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Load the hips low with the spine parallel to the ground or tilted slightly upward, keeping the knees deeply bent over the toes like loaded springs.
rows.fault_trigger: "Tail-Skying". Pre-setting the stance with the hips significantly higher than the shoulders, which forces the fullback to step straight up on the snap and lose all low-man leverage.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a low, explosive center of gravity optimized entirely to clear the line of scrimmage instantly and deliver crushing blocks on linebackers.
Ensure the initial step travels on a direct, explosive downhill path to accelerate rapidly toward the designated mesh point.
Keep the shoulders completely square to the line of scrimmage, leaning the upper body slightly forward to press the track downhill.
rows.fault_trigger: Popping the Top. Straightening the spine and standing tall on the first step, which raises the target area for defenders and kills forward momentum.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The exact moment the step lands, raise the inside arm (closest to the quarterback) to form the top shelf of the ball pocket.
Simultaneously cup the outside hand across the lower abdomen to complete a perfect, wide target for the handoff exchange.
Drive the outside foot sharply across the body at a precise diagonal angle to travel horizontally across the formation.
rows.fault_trigger: Rounding the Track. Taking a looping, curved step backward before crossing face, which alters the mesh timing and allows edge defenders to disrupt the exchange.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Push laterally off the outside edge of the shoe, keeping the hips uncoiled and strictly square to the sideline.
Stay tightly aligned to the quarterback's hip level to execute a smooth read-option or zone track exchange.
Keep the hands wide and clean to present an easy pocket for the quarterback while keeping peripheral vision on edge defenders.
rows.fault_trigger: Staring Down the Ball. Focusing entirely on the quarterback's hands instead of keeping peripheral eyes on the shifting defensive line and unblocking edge threats.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Angle the step slightly outward at a 45-degree trajectory if the play is an outside stretch, or straight downhill for an inside run.
Drop the pad level lower than the quarterback's waist during the mesh to hide the path of the ball from second-level linebackers.
Coordinate the first step with a sharp, aggressive backward drive of the elbows.
rows.fault_trigger: Elbow Flaring. Flaring the elbows out wide on the initial burst, exposing the ribs and making it easier for inside blitzers to jar the ball loose.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Prepare to instantly lock the ball away into a secured carriage on the very second step through the mesh.
Push violently off the inside ball of the staggered back foot, driving it forward into a short, punchy 6-to-12 inch step.
rows.fault_trigger: Tail-Dropping. Lowering the hips further at the snap before moving forward, which causes the fullback to sit down and lose all explosive forward momentum.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the departing foot completely low to the grass, visualizing sliding the foot through a low pane of glass rather than lifting it high.
Simultaneously whip the down hand off the turf and drive the elbows back aggressively to counterbalance the leg drive.
Elevate hands into a loaded strike position while keeping the chin tucked, spine flat, and shoulders lower than the oncoming linebacker's numbers.
rows.fault_trigger: Shooting Upright. Popping the head and chest straight up into the air on the first step, exposing the throat and breastplate to an easy wrecking block by the defender.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take an aggressive forward step toward the assigned protection gap to meet the blitzer inside the pocket perimeter.
rows.fault_trigger: "Catching" the Blitzer. Standing static at the line and waiting for the defender to make contact, allowing them to easily bull-rush the back straight into the quarterback.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Uncoil the hips forward and upward directly out of the 3-point stance to attack the interior rusher at the line of scrimmage.
Take a lateral or diagonal departure step to strictly track the target's inside shoulder on an inside-out angle.
rows.fault_trigger: Over-running the Angle. Charging directly at where the defender is pre-snap rather than tracking their movement, causing a total miss if the defender scrapes inside.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode forward out of the 3-point stance with a low, sliding first step that cleanly clears the turf.
Raise the inside arm (closest to the QB) parallel to the ground at chest height, keeping the elbow strictly bent at 90 degrees.
Run at a wide, lateral angle to out-leverage the defense to the perimeter.
Establish and maintain a strict alignment position exactly 4 yards outside and 1 yard behind the quarterback's tracking path.
rows.fault_trigger: "Trailing Too Tight". Running directly behind or parallel to the quarterback, which destroys the pitch angle and allows one defender to play both threats.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Plant hard on the outside foot to establish a firm base for the lateral transfer.
Drop the hip level low on the step immediately prior to the cut to establish a stable, heavy center of gravity.
Maintain a full, natural sprinting stride while approaching the designated turning point.
rows.fault_trigger: Chopping Strides. Shortening the steps unnecessarily, which kills the back's top-end speed and lets pursuit players catch up.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Plant hard with the foot opposite the desired direction to drive the body horizontally sideways.
rows.fault_trigger: Jumping Too High. Hopping vertically into the air rather than horizontally, which leaves the back suspended and helpless against waiting linebackers.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower the pad level significantly beneath the defender's waist armor to establish dominant leverage.
Sink the hips deeply, widening the base past shoulder-width to brace for heavy impact.
Keep the chest up and eyes locked squarely on the blitzing defender's core.
rows.fault_trigger: Lunging / Bending at the Waist. Diving forward with the head down, making it effortless for an athletic blitzer to execute a quick side-step or swim move.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver a violent, upward two-handed strike squarely inside the chest plate.
Immediately chatter the feet upon impact to reset the anchor and continuously absorb the defender's momentum.
Lift the down hand cleanly and rapidly to clear the dirt and join the strike sequence.
Maintain a wide, stable base with the knees deeply bent, ensuring the spine remains flat.
Drive the palms hard directly into the defender's armpits, lifting upward to disrupt their center of gravity.
rows.fault_trigger: Dropping the Head. Losing sight of the target right before contact, causing the fullback to completely miss the block.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Run the feet aggressively through the contact zone to stall the rusher's vertical tracks completely.
Drop the pad level low during the approach, maintaining a coiled, athletic posture before contact.
Keep the base wide and the feet moving on parallel tracks to dynamically adjust to any late defensive movement or scraping.
Shoot the hands tightly inside the defender's frame, locking onto the jersey cloth to control the block.
rows.fault_trigger: Soft Contact. Using an arm-swipe or hitting with the shoulder instead of shooting the hands, resulting in a weak block that the defender easily sheds.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Run the feet forcefully, either horizontally or vertically, to completely seal the designated running lane.
Maintain absolute horizontal trajectory; do not lift the head or shoulders prematurely into the hole.
Fit the forehead precisely right below the defender's chin strap to establish ultimate low-man leverage.
Shoot the hands forcefully upward directly into the defender's chest plate.
Keep the feet wide and drive them with high-knee, powerful movements to roll the defender vertically back out of the hole.
rows.fault_trigger: Pop and Stop. Landing a heavy initial collision but instantly stopping all foot movement, which lets the defender bounce off and make the tackle. Also: Narrow Track - bringing the feet close together right before contact, making the fullback top-heavy and easy to tip over.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the outside arm tightly across the belt line with the palm cupped upward, completely closing the bottom of the pocket.
Maintain a wide, stable pocket, allowing the quarterback to place the ball firmly into the stomach.
rows.fault_trigger: Staring at the Exchange. Looking down at the quarterback's hands instead of keeping eyes up-field to read the defensive front and blocking keys.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: The instant the ball is seated, clamp both arms tightly over the ball to secure it against the midsection.
rows.fault_trigger: "Clamping down" Early. Snapping the arms shut before the ball is completely seated in the midsection, causing fumbles or bobbles.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fluidly transition the clamped ball into a standard high-and-tight carriage, keeping the eyes continuously up-field to read the blocking keys.
Keep the shoulders turned slightly back toward the quarterback while running to track the pitch smoothly.
Extend the hands away from the body with fingers spread wide and thumbs together to create a massive catching target.
rows.fault_trigger: Body Catching. Letting the spinning football hit the chest plate instead of catching it cleanly with extended hands.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Look the spinning football completely into the hands, physically tracking it with the eyes.
rows.fault_trigger: Turning the Head Early. Looking down-field to check for defenders before the ball is securely caught, leading to a dropped pitch or a muffed fumble.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Look the ball securely down into a five-point tuck before instantly bursting vertically up-field.
Keep the hands up at chest level, palms facing the quarterback, forming a natural, permanent target framework.
rows.fault_trigger: Unprepared Hands. Running with the arms swinging naturally instead of keeping them extended in a ready posture to catch the pitch.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Upon the sudden arrival of the pitch, squeeze the ball firmly with the fingers rather than letting it bounce off the palms.
Secure the ball instantly into a high-and-tight carriage to protect it from impending edge collisions.
Prepare to immediately turn up-field and absorb or deliver an edge hit the moment the ball is secured.
Lift and forcefully drive the opposite leg across the body's midline to slide laterally into the adjacent gap.
rows.fault_trigger: Tripping. Crossing the feet too tightly or low to the turf, causing the back to catch their own cleats and stumble.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the shoulders completely square to the line of scrimmage throughout the entirety of the lateral glide.
rows.fault_trigger: Hip Turning. Turning the entire chest and hips toward the sideline, slowing down forward speed and opening the back to edge hits.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Plant the crossing foot firmly into the turf upon completing the lateral transition.
Instantly transition back into a vertical, downhill sprint without losing baseline forward speed.
Plant the outside foot violently on its inside edge, driving all body weight straight into the turf.
rows.fault_trigger: "Sticking the Cleat". Planting the foot flat and twisting the knee rather than rolling onto the inside instep, which can cause joint injuries or slips.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Push aggressively off that planted foot to physically uncoil the hips.
Clamp the ball tightly against the ribs to ensure it does not flare out during the heavy gravitational shift.
rows.fault_trigger: Elbow Flaring. Letting the football slip away from the ribs during the heavy plant, inviting a defender to strip it.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Explode vertically straight into the newly opened open seam to cut back against the defensive flow.
Drop the inside shoulder slightly toward the direction of the cut to initiate a natural, inward body lean.
rows.fault_trigger: Leaning Outward. Tilting the upper body away from the turn, which ruins balance and causes a wide, looping path.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Apply extra pressure strictly to the outside edges of the shoes to naturally steer the track around the curve.
Execute the curve without chopping the feet or relying on a hard, jarring plant.
Accelerate fully out of the bend to outrun the pursuit angle.
Leave the ground completely, wrapping the ball tightly with two hands while airborne to protect it from sudden contact.
Ensure the jump carries the back horizontally to reset the path one full gap over to clear the pile-up.
Land with a wide, loaded base squarely on the balls of the feet.
rows.fault_trigger: Narrow Landing. Landing with the feet close together, making it impossible to immediately accelerate post-cut.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Instantly drive the knees forward upon landing to immediately resume sprinting.
Maintain a wide driving base on the approach to generate maximum launching power.
rows.fault_trigger: Landing Flat. Falling flat onto the chest without driving the feet, causing the back's momentum to stop exactly where contact was made.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Take a long, powerful final step, launching the torso forward aggressively while keeping the chin strictly tucked.
Keep the ball secured tightly to the ribs with both hands throughout the lunge sequence.
Extend the ball safely over the line or marker at the absolute final microsecond, strictly after the line of scrimmage has been breached.
rows.fault_trigger: Premature Extension. Reaching the ball out too early before passing the line of scrimmage, allowing a defender to easily punch it away.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Squeeze the distance down strictly to 1-2 yards from the defender before executing the launch.
Pivot sharply on the inside foot the exact moment the ball is snapped.
Take a rapid open-step backward off the snap.
Sell the first 3 steps horizontally as a standard flat or swing route.
Sprint diagonally at a 45-degree angle toward the B-gap/C-gap for 3-4 strides.
Engage or simulate a firm pass-block on an interior rusher for a full "one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two" count.
rows.fault_trigger: "Leaking Out Early". Slipping away before the pass rush develops, alerting the linebackers prematurely.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Burst directly out of the stance, tracking tightly through the open A or B-gap.
rows.fault_trigger: Slowing Down at the Line. Reluctantly entering the LOS traffic, which completely disrupts the timing of the deep pass.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Aim your front shoulder directly at the thigh pad or knee line of the oncoming defender.
rows.fault_trigger: "Telegraphing the Cut". Lowering the pad level too early or staring at the defender's shins before launching, alerting them to brace or swim.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Launch horizontally across the defender's frame, physically throwing your body sideways.
rows.fault_trigger: "Diving at the Ankles". Throwing the body too low or too early, allowing the defender to easily step over the block or swat the back down without breaking stride.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ensure the back or side of your shoulder connects with their legs to force the takedown.
rows.fault_trigger: Leading with the Head. Launching head-first into a defender's knees, creating a dangerous risk for neck and concussive injuries.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the head up and eyes locked entirely on the target through the entirety of the strike to protect the neck.
Sprint directly outward toward the numbers on the sideline.
rows.fault_trigger: "Drifting Down-field". Curving the route forward into the linebackers rather than running flat to the sideline, allowing under-coverage defenders to close the window.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a strict depth of 1 to 2 yards past the line of scrimmage, running parallel to the line.
Snap the head back toward the quarterback exactly after the third stride.
rows.fault_trigger: Turning for the Ball Late. Running with the head down and failing to look for the ball until hitting the boundary, causing drops.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep the hands active and eyes wide to secure the ball in stride.
Execute a shallow, curved acceleration path strictly behind the line of scrimmage.
rows.fault_trigger: "Rounding Too Flat". Flattening out the route too early, bringing the back into the path of an unblocked edge rusher.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a constant depth of 2 to 3 yards deep in the backfield while hitting top speed.
rows.fault_trigger: Losing Depth. Floating toward the line of scrimmage while running laterally, which narrows the throwing lane.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Turn the chest back toward the quarterback while maintaining a full lateral stride.
Secure the ball out in front of the body's frame before planting to turn up the sideline.
Plant the outside foot violently to arrest lateral momentum.
Snap the hips vertically, aiming exactly 1 yard inside the sideline boundary.
rows.fault_trigger: "Banana Routing". Rounding the vertical turn in a wide, looping circle, giving trail defenders time to recover.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Accelerate straight down-field to blow past the biting flat defender.
Look back over the inside shoulder to track the deep touch pass.
Plant the outside foot hard and strictly sink the hips to kill outward momentum.
Cut back sharply at an inside 45-degree angle straight across the formation.
rows.fault_trigger: "Rounding the Break". Drifting through the inward turn instead of making a sharp cut, allowing the defender to maintain their cushion.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Present an open, chest-facing target directly between the hash marks.
Ensure the reception phase happens at a strict depth of 3-4 yards past the line of scrimmage.
rows.fault_trigger: Cutting Too Shallow. Breaking backward into the line of scrimmage, clouding the throwing window with defensive linemen.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slip off the block laterally or drop backward slightly to detach.
Keep the body hidden behind the defensive line while extending the hands to form a catch pocket.
rows.fault_trigger: Staring Down the QB. Facing the quarterback with flat feet while waiting, which alerts defenders and stalls the forward track.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the ball and transition instantly into a high-and-tight five-point tuck.
Immediately locate and trail the hip of the pulling center or guard up-field.
Cleanly avoid all interior line wash without slowing momentum.
rows.fault_trigger: "Running Into Traffic". Running directly into an interior zone defender rather than searching out the open void.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Accelerate vertically, establishing a straight track roughly 2 yards outside the hash mark.
Keep eyes completely up-field to read the depth of the interior safety.
Adjust running speed to catch a bullet pass in the seam void or track a touch pass over a linebacker's head.
Secure the snap completely from the center before initiating any rotational movement.
rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Clear the Center. Whipping around too fast before completely securing the snap, resulting in an immediate center-exchange fumble.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint laterally along the line of scrimmage, aggressively riding the line rather than retreating.
rows.fault_trigger: "Floating" Away From the Line. Drifting backward into the backfield while running laterally, which closes down the pitch angle and lets one defender tackle both the QB and the RB.
